rows.original: The road curves around the mountain, carved into a misshapen crag to your east. Your footing is fair and the crag offers you some respite from the howling winds of the mountain, but the snow is treacherous and impedes you with every step. Porous caves dot the peak of the crag, and scattered about the entrance to each one is a set of bones – far too many for any one single creature, surely. Hopefully. You look to the skies and note that the harpies of the peak are deliberately giving the caves – and the road you're on – a wide berth. That's all the reason you need to hurry yourself along and get to your destination. [var0 |[var1 |In the [dayNight |harsh snowblinding light of the sun |pale, crisp light of the moon ], you make out the carcass of a tree jutting from the crag and looming over the road above you. It's been stripped clean of all the leaves, pines, and bark it might have had; if nothing else, it makes for a fine landmark– As you walk underneath it, you feel something suddenly tighten against your ankle and pull taut. Your body shifts to your right, and you hear the sound of a rope, or maybe a whip, snapping into place above you, and your foot lurches upward. You've walked right into a tripwire trap, camouflaged in the snow, and it's trying to throw you up into the air by your foot! You, however, [silly |are simply built different |are stronger than that ]: although the trap caught you by surprise and it knocked you off your footing temporarily, your strength is greater than the rope's, and you stomp your foot back into the snow, keeping it planted firmly on the ground. You can hear the tree above you creak and groan as some counterweight you can't see tries to yank you out of place. With a quick swipe of your [pc.weapon], the rope is cut; your foot is freed; and the tree above you swings upright as all the weight and force is instantly relieved at once. |In the [dayNight |harsh snowblinding light of the sun |pale, crisp light of the moon ], you make out the carcass of a tree jutting from the crag and looming over the road above you. It's been stripped clean of all the leaves, pines, and bark it might have had; if nothing else, it makes for a fine landmark– As you walk underneath it, you feel something suddenly tighten against your ankle and pull taut. Your body shifts to your right, and you hear the sound of a rope, or maybe a whip, snapping into place above you, and your foot lurches upward. You've walked right into a tripwire trap, camouflaged in the snow, and it's trying to throw you up into the air by your foot! You, however, are [silly |simply built different |faster than that ]: although the trap caught you by surprise, your reflexes are honed well enough that, the very moment you see the rope pull taut in the snow, you manage to unsheathe your [pc.weapon] and give it a fierce swipe, cutting it before it has a chance to fling you upward. The lousy rope swings upward, flung by the force of some hidden counterweight, and the tree above you suddenly snaps into place as the rope dangles uselessly from one of its limbs. |In the [dayNight |harsh snowblinding light of the sun |pale, crisp light of the moon ], you make out the carcass of a tree jutting from the crag and looming over the road above you. It's been stripped clean of all the leaves, pines, and bark it might have had; if nothing else, it makes for a fine landmark, but your focus is on– You stop suddenly[party.solo | | and you raise your left fist up above your shoulder, signaling for [party.som | |[comp1.name] |your companions ] to stop as well ]. There's something unnatural about the way that tree is hanging off the crag. It's like it weighs a little too much for itself: the tips of its branches are sagging down just slightly, but the rest of the trunk has a stiffer, firmer form. Something is off. It's hard to see against the snow, [dayNight |especially with the sun reflecting off the whiteness and shining into your eyes |especially when you're just going by the light of the moon in otherwise total darkness ], but you manage to make out a long, taut line of rope that's been cleverly camouflaged to be packed with snow against snow and left naked against craggy rock or dried bark. You can see where it disappears into the snow covering the road you're on, but you can't see where, exactly, it is on the road – whether it's one step in front of you or twenty, or if it's just under the surface or right against the gravel. Cautiously, you slip your [pc.weapon]'s end into the snow, where you think the rope is– And suddenly, there's the sound of a branch snapping; a thin line of snow lurches upward in front of you; you see the tree above you shift back into place, its wood groaning from the exertion; and you feel something whip against your [pc.weapon], unseen under the snow and moving with enough velocity that, if you weren't already on-guard from the suspicion, it would have knocked it clean out of your hand. ] As quickly as it all happens, a mound of snow on the far side of the road suddenly erupts, as if something buried beneath it had exploded. The sound of a warrior's yell pierces the winds of the mountaintop, and a flurry of something large and covered in white fur, brandishing a spear, comes charging straight toward you. But the excitement winds down just as quickly as it starts up: the warrior that had burst from the snow stops just a few paces after starting, and once they realize that a mistake's been made, they lower their weapon. "You are not the prey I hunt," a voice says – gruff and lower in pitch, but undeniably feminine. "Beit dorr ei wikt," she whispers under her breath. It's difficult to get a look at the finer details of the woman [dayNight |with the sun reflecting off both the snow and her white fur so harshly, |with the night being what it is – you can hardly see your hand in front of your face – ] but you can see that she's undeniably a vulperine; her fur is stark white, which blends her in well with her snowy surroundings[dayNight |, especially in the middle of the day ], but she's also covered in dark blue lines of markings surrounding her thighs, torso, and face; and she's wearing vanishingly little clothing... although her fur is so pompous and fluffy that she barely needs to. "It is good that you did not fall to my trap," the warrior woman says as she approaches you. The weapon in her hand, a staff significantly longer than she is tall and capped with a gleaming metal point, flips into a backhanded grip, with the tip behind her body and pointed upward, showing that she means no harm. Despite her words, though, you can tell from the scowl on her face and the intensity of her gait that she's not in a particularly happy mood. "But you did not need to break it." [pc.isDK |You don't respond at all. This woman is acting like you did something to her; if you had stepped into that trap, you would have been thrown against the crag wall like your [pc.weapon] was, if not something else. You don't owe her shit. With a huff, she |You justify your actions by saying that you spotted the trap, but you couldn't make out the intricacies: you knew something was amiss but you couldn't see how to disarm it, or how to get around it. You did what you thought was safest for yourself[party.som | | and [comp1.name] | and your friends ]. "I do not care," she says with a huff as she ] goes to the rope, now dangling listlessly from the tree overhead with nothing caught in its noose-snare at its end. She reaches down into the snow, bare-handed, where the rope disappears, and unwinds it from an anchor she had hidden on the road. "My prey will have heard of this and will not come to this spot. I must start my hunt fresh." [pc.isDK |You suggest that maybe she ought to be more proactive. The other vulperine hunters of the mountain are out there hunting their prey directly; she's here, waiting with a trap, hoping that her prey will come to her. The others seem to get more frequent results. "You do not know what you say," she spits as she coils the rope |Whatever it is you did to her trap and her 'hunt,' you didn't mean it; like you said, you were just looking out for yourself. If she needed help with tracking something down, maybe you could– "This is not for a taminyk to say," she interrupts as she coils the rope ] around her right elbow and wrist, wrapping the rope around her arm in an oval shape. "You knew the trap was set, yet you did not leave it be. You are not skilled for the hunt. My prey would eat you whole.[pc.ra kitsune |" She eyes your body, and her nose crinkles as she takes a few sniffs of the air. "And to make it all worse, you stink of Keros! It is not a shock that a wrick kimna-wuute would be so rash. ]" [pc.isDK |Taking some offense to her assumptions, you tell her that y |Y ]ou certainly doubt that: with all the things you've been through so far, you think you could handle some dumb animal, or whatever it is she's hunting. "That is what they thought as well," she responds, pointing the tip of her spear towards the caves dotting the crag's distance wall – and the piles of bones scattered about their entrances. "I hunt a prey that is not like any other. No other hunter has the skill or the guts to hunt what I hunt." [pc.isDK |She calls it courage; if all the other hunters, and all of the harpies, and all of the creatures who are now all just a pile of bones sitting in front of some caves, couldn't bring down whatever those animals are, then maybe what she's doing isn't courageous. Maybe it's something else. |The fact that she's hunting by herself – and that the harpies are giving this part of the mountain a wide berth – tells you that maybe she ought to be a little more prepared than she is now. She's a lone hunter going against something, or many somethings, vicious enough to kill a whole slew of... whatever those bones used to be, and she's hoping to do it by herself with a spear and some rope. ] She 'tch's at your words as she rounds up the last of the rope, putting its end in her palm and closing her fingers around it. "[var2 |You had come from the south, so you no doubt seek the harps and their home |You had come from the north, so you have gone 'round the hill top ]," she says, looking towards you. For the first time, you get a good, long look at her deep blue eyes – from the matted fur around her eyes, you get the impression that she's been through a bit more than her abrasive façade lets on. "[var2 |Go on this path and you will find it. I have set no more traps. |There is no thing else for you here, taminyk. Leave this spot when you can. ]" With that, she brushes past you and makes her way south, towards the vulperine village that you had passed by on the way up the mountain. |In the [dayNight |harsh snowblinding light of the sun |pale, crisp light of the moon ], you make out the carcass of a tree jutting from the crag and looming over the road above you. It's been stripped clean of all the leaves, pines, and bark it might have had; if nothing else, it makes for a fine landmark, but your focus is getting out of here and back to civilization as quickly as you can. Your boots tromp through the snow, the fluffy powder making a satisfying crunch under your weight with every step. You[party.som | | and [comp1.name] | and your companions ] keep your eyes peeled around you for any sudden movements; you're a foreigner that's out of [pc.hisHer] element, and you– Just as you pass underneath the dead tree, you hear the sound of a branch snapping; you see a thin line in the snow suddenly lurch upward; you feel a tight, sharp pain in your right ankle; and out of the corner of your eye, you see the tree above you start to shift, its whole body springing upright. Before you can register what's happening, you're knocked onto your side and you're whipped straight up into the air, flinging upward nearly a dozen feet before swinging around helplessly like a clapper in a bell. Before your senses can come back to you[party.som | | and [comp1.name] can come to your aid | and your companions can either help you or ready themselves for an ambush ], a nearby mound of snow erupts like something within it had burst. The sound of a warrior yelling a battle cry echoes off the craggy wall behind you, and you happen to catch the glint of a sharpened weapon [dayNight |against the bright snow |in the moon's light ] headed straight for you! [party.solo |You're left dangling by your right foot, helpless in the face of this new threat, because you didn't have the wordly wherewithal to notice the trap hidden among the snow |[party.has Arona Atugia Brint Quintillus |Rather than try to cut you down, [comp1.name] readies [comp1.hisHer] [comp1.weapon], prepared to face down whatever this threat is[party.has Agnimitra Azzyran Brienne Cait Etheryn Kiyoko Viviane |, while ] |Faced with either assisting you or turning to face whatever this new threat is, ][party.has Agnimita Azzyran Brienne Cait Etheryn Kiyoko Viviane | [comp2.name] puts [comp2.himHer]self between you and it protectively, [comp2.hisHer] arms raised defensively to try and block whatever it is that's coming towards [comp2.himHer] ] ]. But just as quickly as the excitement happens, it all stops again, and whatever it was that had burst out of the snow mound screaming bloody murder comes to a halt. "Tch," you hear someone sneer contemptibly at the sight of you. You're still hanging upside-down and you're still swinging and bouncing on whatever rope has snared you; you don't have a clear sight on who, or what, is approaching you. "Taminyk ei humnah. You are not the prey I hunt." [party.solo |You struggle a bit to try and get a better look who it is that's caught you so unawares, but with you in the position your in, your options are somewhat limited. You could get yourself down if you had a bit of time, but you're dizzy and vulnerable; if this warrior wanted you dead, they would have pierced you through by now. |[party.has Arona |"Back off, you psycho bitch!" Arona yells, thrusting the head of her hammer towards the warrior, less as an attack and more as a threat. "We were walking, here! The fuck's wrong with you?!" |[party.som | |[comp1.name] remains nonplussed and ready: despite the warrior's suddenly-calmer demeanor, things had been moving quickly, and if there's ever a time to stay on-guard, it's now. |[comp1.name] remains nonplussed and ready, with [comp2.name] repeatedly looking over her shoulder to make sure that you're not in any more distress than you are right now. Although the warrior is taking a calmer demeanor, things had been moving quickly in a short amount of time, and tension is high. ] ] ] "I mean no harm," the warrior says. From the sound of their voice, you can tell that it's a woman, albeit a bit on the gruffer side. You still can't get a good look at her, though. "[party.solo |I will let you down." You look down at your ankle again. The tripwire trap she had set up is expertly made: although it's a simple hemp rope, the knot around your ankle would take quite some time to undo with your fingers, and hacking away at it with something sharp would be dangerous to your own foot, never mind the distance you'd fall. You're not about to go anywhere, and you're not in a combative position; you have no choice but to trust her. |I will let you–" You can hear the sound of her taking a step in the snow, and [comp1.name] refuses to budge; she's not going to get near you without first going through [comp1.himHer]. "[pc.dcb |Hold on," you say to [comp1.name]. "Is she hot?" A minor pause. "[party.has Agnimita Arona Brint Quintillus |She's not bad, yeah." |I mean... I suppose?" ] "Then it's okay," you say. "Let her cut me down." |Let her do it," you say, although your voice doesn't exactly sound as inspiring as you had hoped, given your predicament. "We're not exactly in the best of positions, here. I don't want to start a fight." |No, no," you insist, wagging your arms and kicking your free leg to try and turn around to see the woman. "She sounds hot. I'm into a hottie that knows her way around a rope! Let her cut me down!" ] [comp1.name] hesitates, then steps aside on your instruction, letting the woman approach. ] You feel a gentle but firm hand on your shoulder, spinning you around – and you're suddenly face-to-face with a snow-white muzzle of a vulperine woman. Her dark blue eyes are commanding, but still gentle: from her eyes alone, she looks like the kind of woman that[pc.isDK | still has a few fucks left to give, but she's being very selective about it |'s been in predicaments like this one before, and knows exactly how to deal with it, provided you do what she says ]. In her right hand is a long, ornate spear with a gleaming metal tip; she's holding it in a reverse-grip, so that the spearhead is pointed up and behind her arm, showing that she's not in an aggressive stance. [pc.ra kitsune |When the vulperine woman looks at you, however, she pauses, and then her nose visibly crinkles, the disgust reaching her eyes and then some. "You are a wrick kimna-wuute? A kitsune? You are slave to Keros?" You aren't sure if you agree with her word choice, but... well, it's not like you're trying to hide it, exactly. You confirm that you're beholden to Keros. She pauses, then sighs through her nose as she walks past you, spinning you around on the rope so you can see where she's going. |Her eyes narrow on yours for a moment, scanning you and your face. Her nose crinkles upward slightly as she catches a whiff of your scent. "I have done you wrong," she says curtly before walking past you, spinning you around on the rope so you can see where she's going. ] When she reaches the foot of the craggy surface, she roots through the snow, easily finding where she had planted the lead of the rope. [pc.ra kitsune |With a quick, precise swing of her spear, the weapon cuts into the rope – and suddenly, all that tension keeping you suspended in the air is gone, and you're sent plummeting several feet straight into the ground, head-first. Fortunately, the snow is soft and yielding, cushioning your impact, but even still, it's left a bump on your head and a pain in your back that's going to take a while to mend out. |Reaching into the snow with her bare fingers, she finds the rock anchor she had tied the lead around, unwinding it again and again until the only thing keeping you suspended in the air is her own strength of arm. She gently lowers you to the ground until you can reach up and touch the snow, and from there, your lower body hits the ground relatively painlessly once she eases her grip. ] "[var2 |You had come from the south, so you no doubt seek the harps and their home |You had come from the north, so you have already come 'round the hill top ]," the woman says as she rolls up the rope, wrapping it around her right elbow and shoulder to coil it into an oval. "[var0 |Go on this path and you will find it. I have set no more traps. |There is no thing else for you here, taminyk. Leave this spot when you can. ]" [pc.isDK |She sounds a little perturbed... but she was the one that laid a trap that got you strung up in the first place. You're not about to apologize. If she was so determined to capture something specific, she ought to have stopped you when you approached. She says nothing further as she finishes wrapping up the rope around her arm and heading south, towards the vulperine village you had passed by on the way up the mountain. |As you pull yourself to your feet and brush off the snow clinging to your body, you note that she sounds upset[pc.ra kitsune |. And that she has a bone to pick with anyone affiliated with Keros ]. "My hunt is no more," she confirms bitterly. "My prey is too smart; it will have heard you trip the trap, and it will not come back to this spot. My hunt is no more, and it is your fault." Well, that's hardly fair: it's not exactly your fault that she left out a trap and you got caught in it. If she was so determined to capture this thing, she should have stopped you somehow. "And show my self," she states, her lips curling in frustration at your words. "You know no thing. I will set my trap here, taminyk.; it will not be now or the next day. Watch your pace the next time you are here." With that, she finishes rolling the rope around her arm, and she makes her way south, towards the vulperine village you had passed by on the way up the mountain. ] ]
rows.translation: 道路沿着山势蜿蜒而行，在你的东侧形成了那些崎岖不平的岩壁。你的足部步还算稳当，这些岩壁也能为你遮挡山风带来的肆虐，但积雪却非常危险，每走一步都会给你带来阻碍。 多孔的洞穴遍布这座峭壁的顶端，而在每个洞穴的入口处，都散落着一堆骨头——数量之多，显然不可能是某一种生物留下的。但愿如此吧。 你抬头望向天空，发现那些栖息在山顶的鹰身女妖们似乎有意地避开了这些洞穴，也避开了你正在行走的道路。 这就是你为什么需要加快速度，尽快到达目的地的原因。 [var0 |[var1 |在……之中 [dayNight |刺眼的阳光 |清冷而明亮的月光 ]你可以看到有一棵树的树干从岩石中伸出，耸立在上方的道路上。它的叶子、松针和树皮早已被完全剥落；不过，即便没有这些附属物，它也依然是一个很好的地标。 当你从它下方走过时，突然感到有什么东西紧紧抓住了你的足部踝，将其拉紧。你的身体向右侧倾斜，同时听到头顶上有一根绳子——或者也许是一根鞭子——被猛地拉紧的声音，紧接着你的足部就被猛地向上拽去。 你刚刚踏入了一个隐藏在雪中的陷阱，这个陷阱正试图抓住你的足部，将你抛向空中！ 然而，你…… [silly |它们的构造本身就是不同的。 |比那要强大得多 ]虽然那个陷阱让你措手不及，暂时让你失去了平衡，但你的力量比那根绳子要大得多。你用力将足部踩在雪地上，让双足部牢牢地固定在地面上。你可以听到头顶上的树木发出吱嘎声和呻吟声——那些你看不见的配重正在试图把你从那里拉出来。你迅速地…… [pc.weapon]绳子被切断了，你的足部也被解放了，你头顶上的树也恢复了直立状态——因为所有的重量和力量都瞬间消失了。 |在……中 [dayNight |刺眼的阳光 |柔和而清亮的月光 ]你可以看到有一棵树的树干从岩石中伸出，耸立在你上方的道路上。它的叶子、松针和树皮早已被完全剥落；不过，即便没有这些附属物，它也依然是一个很好的地标。 当你从它下方走过时，突然感到有什么东西紧紧抓住了你的足部踝，将其拉紧。你的身体向右侧倾斜，同时听到头顶上有一根绳子——或者也许是一根鞭子——被猛地拉紧的声音，紧接着你的足部就被猛地向上拽去。 你刚刚走进了一个隐藏在雪中的陷阱，这个陷阱正试图抓住你的足部，把你抛到空中！ 不过，你…… [silly |设计理念完全不同 |快得连那个都比不上。 ]虽然那个陷阱让你措手不及，但你的反应能力已经训练得相当出色了，因此当你在雪地上看到绳子被拉紧的那一瞬间，你立刻拔出了刀。 [pc.weapon] 你猛地一挥，就在那根绳子有机会将你甩向高空之前将其斩断。那根破旧的绳子在某种隐藏的配重的作用下向上摆动，而你头顶上的树木也突然恢复了原状，只剩下那根绳子无用地悬挂在它的树枝上。 |在……中 [dayNight |刺眼的阳光 |清冷而明亮的月光 ]你看到有一棵树的树干从岩石中伸出，耸立在你上方的道路上。它的叶子、松针和树皮早已被剥落殆尽；即便没有其他作用，它也算是一个明显的地标，但你的注意力此刻集中在…… 你突然停下了足部步。[party.solo | | 然后你将左拳举过肩膀，以此发出信号。 [party.som | |[comp1.name] |你的同伴 ] 也停下来吧 ]那棵树悬挂在岩石上的样子显得很不自然。它的重量似乎有点超过了自身的承受能力：树枝的末端微微下垂，而树干的其他部分却依然保持着挺直的状态。显然有些地方不对劲。 在雪的覆盖下，这些异常之处很难被察觉。 [dayNight |尤其是当阳光照射在那些洁白的事物上，反射出来的光芒会直射进你的眼睛时。 |尤其是在其他地方一片漆黑的情况下，你只能依靠月光来前行时。 ]你努力观察着，终于发现了一条长长的、绷得紧紧的绳子。这条绳子被巧妙地伪装了起来：在积雪的地方，它就与雪融为一体；而在岩石或干枯的树皮上，它则裸露在外。你可以看到它消失在你们所走道路上的积雪中，但却无法确定它具体位于道路的哪个位置——是就在你前方一步的地方，还是二十步之外；是埋在积雪下面，还是紧贴着碎石。 你小心翼翼地，将手伸了进去…… rows.raw: " The road curves around the mountain, carved into a misshapen crag to your east. Your footing is fair and the crag offers you some respite from the howling winds of the mountain, but the snow is treacherous and impedes you with every step. Porous caves dot the peak of the crag, and scattered about the entrance to each one is a set of bones – far too many for any one single creature, surely. Hopefully. You look to the skies and note that the harpies of the peak are deliberately giving the caves – and the road you're on – a wide berth. That's all the reason you need to hurry yourself along and get to your destination. [var0 |[var1 |In the [dayNight |harsh snowblinding light of the sun |pale, crisp light of the moon ], you make out the carcass of a tree jutting from the crag and looming over the road above you. It's been stripped clean of all the leaves, pines, and bark it might have had; if nothing else, it makes for a fine landmark– As you walk underneath it, you feel something suddenly tighten against your ankle and pull taut. Your body shifts to your right, and you hear the sound of a rope, or maybe a whip, snapping into place above you, and your foot lurches upward. You've walked right into a tripwire trap, camouflaged in the snow, and it's trying to throw you up into the air by your foot! You, however, [silly |are simply built different |are stronger than that ]: although the trap caught you by surprise and it knocked you off your footing temporarily, your strength is greater than the rope's, and you stomp your foot back into the snow, keeping it planted firmly on the ground. You can hear the tree above you creak and groan as some counterweight you can't see tries to yank you out of place. rows.original: Kailani, like the others in the vulperine village, lives in a simple one-story hut made of stone that's been caulked with mud, with the roof being mostly made of a few wooden beams and dressed with straw. There's no floor; it's naked ground that's been thoroughly stamped flat and smooth from many years, maybe generations, of people constantly walking on it. It's very rustic and low on the amenities you had come to expect from civilian life, and it doesn't have a front door or even a sheet to provide the first of the hut's three rooms any privacy – but, to its credit, it's much warmer inside it than you had expected. All that caulked mud provides good insulation. The hut is fairly large for what you had expected from a village like the vulperines. The first room is the hut's foyer and common room: its 'furniture' amounts to piles of grass and straw clumped together to make something to sit in. The walls are lined with things a huntress like Kailani would be interested in: knives of all shapes and sizes, meant for anything from whittling wood to skinning fresh kills, are set in a meticulous and deliberate order nearer to the hut's entrance; hunting nets lie rolled up in tight bundles by your feet to your left when you enter the hut, with other nets strung up against a backboard in need for repair; set above the door is a hunting bow, its string badly weathered and its wood worn thin from overuse, looking like it might snap the next time an arrow is drawn; and so on. Oddly for a hunter, Kailani owns only one spear[kailani.quested |, not counting the family heirloom that Inaya had you retrieve, which stands on its point across from the hut's entrance, on full display for everyone to see ]. The other two rooms of the hut are bedrooms. What passes for a 'bed' is a raised mound of flattened, caked mud, dressed with straw and covered with two layers of bearskin – plenty warm, but not exactly world-class comfort. The left room is clearly [inaya.introduced |Inaya's |the kit's, or, at least, someone else much smaller than Kailani ]: the bed is smaller; colored pigments lay strewn about, applied to anything from gifted leathers to the very walls; and sitting on the bed is a doll made of fabric that's held together with twine. The right room is Kailani's: the bed is much larger[kailani.isMate |, and there's a crib made of sturdier wood and stones and laid with the softest fabrics and leathers available in the village ], and, like the other room, blue pigments sit in the corner of the room surrounding a bucket filled with clear water, but otherwise, there's not much more to Kailani's room. But that's enough of examining her house. There's plenty to see on Kailani as well. Kailani is a vulperine woman; based on the color of her fur and the energy in her body language, you'd assume her to be somewhere in her early-to-mid twenties. She stands roughly six feet tall; like all vulperine, she's covered head-to-toe in fur, although her boreal race gives her fur some different qualities. Her fur is all white, from head to toe, and it's particularly thick and fluffy in some places, especially around the neck, giving her a majestic mane. The fur on her tail is so bushy that it's bound with straps in two places just to keep it under control, although the straps are worn and torn; she clearly doesn't care all that much. The rest of the fur on her body is thick and shaggy, but not so unkempt that you couldn't dig down and find her skin – or other sensitive parts – with just a little bit of effort. Her matching-hair has grown down to the small of her back, with wild strands of it breaking off from the main clump, giving her a messy look like she hasn't combed it or cut it a single time in her life. Her eyes are a deep, dark blue, and, like all vulperines, she has a canine muzzle on her face. Pockmarked all over her body are tribal tattoos that have been meticulously painted onto the fur, but they're fading in some spots and need to be reapplied. They include circular shapes around her arms and wrists; diamonds and swirls on her thighs; jagged lines going up her stomach; some semicircles on her face and around her eyes[kailani.fucked |; large, thick circles around her boobs ]; and so on. Although it's difficult to make out underneath her fur, her occupation has a hunter has given her toned arms, abdominal muscles[kailani.isShowing | (although you imagine the baby bump in her stomach has made them a little less obvious) ], and especially toned thighs and calves. Despite how thick her fur is, she's not wearing nothing: a top made of thick leather keeps her D-cup breasts in place, and around her waist, she wears a kilt made of a thick, protective mix of fabrics and leathers that reaches down to just above her knees. The top is plain brown all the way across, but the kilt is a mixture of browns, yellows, and greens, with red highlights, and on the front is a fanciful circular design with a sharp arrow pointed up through its center, likely denoting her occupation. She doesn't wear anything on her legs or arms – her fur probably acts as a natural bracer for the bow she owns – but she does wear a pair of thin animal-skin covers on her feet to help her deal with rougher terrain. She has two, thick, primitive belts of leather wrapped around her tail in different places to keep the fluffy fur under control while she's out and about. [kailani.fucked |Between Kailani's legs is a normal vagina, and although her thick fur lightens in density around her stomach, groin, and inner thighs, it's still a journey to find it. Underneath her fluffy tail and between her butt cheeks is her asshole, right where it belongs. You also know that she doesn't wear underwear. |You haven't seen what she's keeping underneath that kilt of hers, but you have a good feeling that, at the very least, she has a butthole between her butt cheeks, where it belongs. ]

The walls are lined with things a huntress like Kailani would be interested in: knives of all shapes and sizes, meant for anything from whittling wood to skinning fresh kills, are set in a meticulous and deliberate order nearer to the hut's entrance; hunting nets lie rolled up in tight bundles by your feet to your left when you enter the hut, with other nets strung up against a backboard in need for repair; set above the door is a hunting bow, its string badly weathered and its wood worn thin from overuse, looking like it might snap the next time an arrow is drawn; and so on. Oddly for a hunter, Kailani owns only one spear[kailani.quested |, not counting the family heirloom that Inaya had you retrieve, which stands on its point across from the hut's entrance, on full display for everyone to see ]. The other two rooms of the hut are bedrooms. What passes for a 'bed' is a raised mound of flattened, caked mud, dressed with straw and covered with two layers of bearskin – plenty warm, but not exactly world-class comfort. The left room is clearly [inaya.introduced |Inaya's |the kit's, or, at least, someone else much smaller than Kailani ]: the bed is smaller; colored pigments lay strewn about, applied to anything from gifted leathers to the very walls; and sitting on the bed is a doll made of fabric that's held together with twine. The right room is Kailani's: the bed is much larger[kailani.isMate |, and there's a crib made of sturdier wood and stones and laid with the softest fabrics and leathers available in the village ], and, like the other room, blue pigments sit in the corner of the room surrounding a bucket filled with clear water, but otherwise, there's not much more to Kailani's room. But that's enough of examining her house. There's plenty to see on Kailani as well. Kailani is a vulperine woman; based on the color of her fur and the energy in her body language, you'd assume her to be somewhere in her early-to-mid twenties. She stands roughly six feet tall; like all vulperine, she's covered head-to-toe in fur, although her boreal race gives her fur some different qualities. Her fur is all white, from head to toe, and it's particularly thick and fluffy in some places, especially around the neck, giving her a majestic mane. The fur on her tail is so bushy that it's bound with straps in two places just to keep it under control, although the straps are worn and torn; she clearly doesn't care all that much. The rest of the fur on her body is thick and shaggy, but not so unkempt that you couldn't dig down and find her skin – or other sensitive parts – with just a little bit of effort. Her matching-hair has grown down to the small of her back, with wild strands of it breaking off from the main clump, giving her a messy look like she hasn't combed it or cut it a single time in her life. Her eyes are a deep, dark blue, and, like all vulperines, she has a canine muzzle on her face. Pockmarked all over her body are tribal tattoos that have been meticulously painted onto the fur, but they're fading in some spots and need to be reapplied. They include circular shapes around her arms and wrists; diamonds and swirls on her thighs; jagged lines going up her stomach; some semicircles on her face and around her eyes[kailani.fucked |; large, thick circles around her boobs ]; and so on. Although it's difficult to make out underneath her fur, her occupation has a hunter has given her toned arms, abdominal muscles[kailani.isShowing | (although you imagine the baby bump in her stomach has made them a little less obvious) ], and especially toned thighs and calves. Despite how thick her fur is, she's not wearing nothing: a top made of thick leather keeps her D-cup breasts in place, and around her waist, she wears a kilt made of a thick, protective mix of fabrics and leathers that reaches down to just above her knees. The top is plain brown all the way across, but the kilt is a mixture of browns, yellows, and greens, with red highlights, and on the front is a fanciful circular design with a sharp arrow pointed up through its center, likely denoting her occupation. She doesn't wear anything on her legs or arms – her fur probably acts as a natural bracer for the bow she owns – but she does wear a pair of thin animal-skin covers on her feet to help her deal with rougher terrain. She has two, thick, primitive belts of leather wrapped around her tail in different places to keep the fluffy fur under control while she's out and about. [kailani.fucked |Between Kailani's legs is a normal vagina, and although her thick fur lightens in density around her stomach, groin, and inner thighs, it's still a journey to find it. Underneath her fluffy tail and between her butt cheeks is her asshole, right where it belongs. You also know that she doesn't wear underwear. |You haven't seen what she's keeping underneath that kilt of hers, but you have a good feeling that, at the very least, she has a butthole between her butt cheeks, where it belongs. ]"

She fixes her hair, ensures that her fur and kilt isn't being obstructed, and then flumps down onto it like she doesn't care if the grass and straw she's sitting on flutters out in every direction as she does. You do mostly the same on the only other thing to sit on – a different pile of straw and grass – but you do it because it's too low to the ground for you to easily sit on. "What is on your mind?" she asks you, crossing her toned legs, resting her elbow on her knee and her chin on the back of her hand. She looks at you with a smile; you have her undivided attention. |You ask Kailani if she'd like to talk. Not about anything in particular; you just want to sit and get to know her a little better. "Yes," she answers, leading you into her hut's common room. She gestures to a pile of clumped straw and grass; as far as you can tell, it's just a pile of shavings she hadn't thrown out yet. "Sit," she says, turning towards a second, similar clump of shavings and, after fixing her hair and ensuring that her fur and kilt aren't being obstructed, takes a seat. Apparently it's a chair. "The hawneio think that our... agh," she grunts through her throat as she struggles with her Belharan, "that our komnifrecht-nim can not last, and that it is best that we speak more with taminyko like you." Kailani crosses her legs; she rests her elbow on her top leg, and then her chin on the back of her hand. Then, she watches you like she's studying you. "Let us speak, then." ]

rows.original: You ask Kailani about her hunting. There are any number of ways she could contribute to her family and to her village; why did she pick being a hunter, of all the possibilities? "I did not choose to hunt, [pc.name]," she answers, leaning back in her pile of grass and straw. "It is a... it is what my home has done. My name is Ibulim Kailani. The word 'ibulim' means 'one that hunts.' My... my umwricht, my, uh, male one that raised me, was a village ibulim. His umfracht, female one that raised him, was a village ibulim. Her umwricht was a village ibulim. And so on." Okay, it's a family 'business,' then. You ask her about her hunting: when you first met her, it was over a trap she had laid in the middle of the road. What was she hunting? It wasn't a person; she said that you weren't her prey. "The 'road' was not where I willed to lay the trap," she recounts, rolling her eyes upward as she recalls that day. "There are caves near the 'road' at that spot. There are bones in front of the caves. I was on the hunt for prey in the caves. That the trap was near the caves was... not good: it is too close to where it rests. I do not know if there is more than one prey." It sounds like she's put a lot of thought into where she puts the trap, and why. Either that, or choosing where to put her traps is like second nature to her now. What more can she tell you about what it is she's hunting? "Two legs," she responds, lifting her left hand out, palm-up, and using her right hand's index and middle fingers to walk across it. "Big. More than me[pc.heightRange 0 96 |. More than you |. Might be more than you ]. But..." She twists her mouth and looks away from you, her expression a mix of frustration and embarrassment. "I have not seen it. I have seen its tracks. It lives in the caves; I am sure of that. But it does not come out while I wait." If she's so sure that something lives in those caves, but she's never seen it go in or come out, then why doesn't she go into the caves to hunt it? She could get a small team together and track it down. "You would not go in the village and hunt a vulp, [pc.name]," she responds, turning her head a bit to look out of the open door to her hut. "There are lots of... there are lots of, uhh," she stutters, gesticulating with her hands as she tries to think of the next word in her sentence. "It would not be good to try. There are lots of vulps in the village. There could be many preys in the caves." Kailani leans to one side, resting on her arm as she leans on the pile of grass and straw to talk with you. "No other vulp will join me. I am the best ibulim in the village, [pc.name]; the bones of the prey's meals lie in front of the caves, as a... as a, ah, a bimlowhtre. 'Do not come in,' the bones say. No other ibulim has the skill – or the guts – to try, and I can not do it alone." That's all interesting to note: according to Kailani, there's something living in the caves of the mountains, and she wants to hunt it down, but it's too smart to come out of the caves while she has traps set up, and going in to hunt it proactively is too dangerous by herself. That's worth keeping in mind. Shifting topics slightly, you ask Kailani how the hunt has been going in general. Not just with whatever prey is in the caves, but the hunt that she does to bring food into the village. You'd have thought that wild game wouldn't be so easy to find in an area as desolate as this. "I go far to hunt my food," she notes. "And the hunt is more than big game. Fish is – uh, there are lots of fish in the lake. I hunt and I fish all the same." But then, her expression clouds over as she looks to the door to her hut. Specifically, her eyes draw upward, toward the bow she has on display: it's old, badly worn, and the string is tattered, looking like it might snap the next time she goes to draw it. "The hunt is too good," she notes, her voice wavering with uneasiness. "The world is... not the same. Omlinawo, or, big meat, do not come this way. Ibulimo go to big meat, but... this has not been true any more. They come to us. The world is not the same and it is... um, the hawneio are..." She gesticulates with her hands some more, her face scrunching up as she stutters through her syllables. "The hawneio are fwricht. They are not well with this change." You think you can understand what she means by 'the world is changing.' Thanks to recent events, the imp and demon populations have been on the rise, which would upset the local animal ecosystems and drive them out of their habitats, forcing them towards people like Kailani and her village.You ask her if the hunters of the village are having a hard time keeping up with the sudden rush of animals. Kailani tilts her head in confusion; all of the fur and hair on her head sways and bobs with the motion. "I do not know what you mean." Like, is there too many animals for them to hunt...? Is there a risk of the game becoming intrusive to their village? She, in response, tilts her head further and squints her eyes. "I had said that the hunt is–" she starts, then her head straightens and her eyes go wide. "Oh! I see what you mean now. The ibulimo are well. There is no threat to us or to the village. But..." With her left hand, she points to a nearby rack with a tanned leather draped over it. It looks fresh. "There is too much meat. There is too much umlifch. There are too much bones. The hunt is not to kill, [pc.name]; the hunt is to eat." Again, she looks sadly at her worn bow above her door. "The omlinawo are here, and they are too much. If we do not hunt, they will graze too much. They will... uh, they will wreck our home. They could hurt our village. But if we hunt too much, meat will rot. There will too few for the next cold. We can not leave; that would make it worse." She sighs and rests her chin on the back of her hand. She looks towards you, but her gaze is a million miles away. "We can not do no thing... but it is hard to do some thing."[pc.isDK | You ask her, point-blank, why she and the other hunters don't hunt the imps and demons that are making things difficult. With skills like hers, at the very least, the imps ought to be easy to deal with. "The hunt is not to kill, [pc.name]," she repeats. "The hunt is to eat." There's a solution to that as well, but... Well, you're out of ideas. ]
rows.translation: 你询问凯拉妮关于她从事狩猎的原因。她有很多方式可以为自己的家庭和村庄做出贡献，那么在所有这些可能性中，她为什么偏偏选择了成为一名猎人呢？ “其实并不是我主动选择了狩猎…… [pc.name]就是这样的，”她回答道，靠在堆满草和稻草的地方说，“这就是我的家乡所做的事情。我的名字是伊布利姆·凯拉尼。‘伊布利姆’这个词语的意思是‘狩猎者’。我的……我的…… 嗯……这个名称听起来有点特别吧。嗯，抚养我长大的那个男性，其实是一个来自村庄的人。 暴食症他的 运费那个抚养他长大的女人，是一个村子里的人。 暴食症她的 乌姆瑞希特 那是一个村庄。 暴食症等等诸如此类的事情。” 好吧，那么这确实是一门家族‘事业’了。如果你问她关于她打猎的事情：当初你们第一次见面时，正是因为她在路上设置了陷阱。她当时在猎什么？显然不是人；她说你根本不是她的猎物。 “那条‘路’，其实并不是我…… 有决心的 设下陷阱，”她回忆道，说着便向上翻了个白眼。“在那个地方，‘道路’附近有一些洞穴，洞穴前面还有骨头。我当时正在那些洞穴里寻找猎物，而陷阱就设在了洞穴附近。……不太好：它的位置离猎物休息的地方太近了。我不知道是否还有其他猎物在那里。 听起来，她在放置陷阱的位置以及选择放置地点的原因上确实花了很多心思。要么就是，对于她来说，选择在哪里放置陷阱已经成了一种下意识的行为。 关于她正在寻找的东西，她还能告诉你些什么呢？ “两条腿，”她回答道，同时抬起左手部，手部掌朝上，然后用右手部的食指和中指在她的手部掌上模拟着两条腿的形状。“很粗壮，比我的手部还要粗。[pc.heightRange 0 96 |比你想象的还要多 |可能对你来说，这是个难以承受的负担。 ]但是……”她扭动着嘴，将目光从你身上移开，脸上的表情既充满了沮丧，又带着尴尬。“我并没有亲眼看到它。我只是看到了它的足迹。它肯定住在洞穴里，这一点我很确定。但是每次我等待的时候，它都不会出现。如果她那么确信那些洞穴里有什么生物存在，却又从未见过它们进出洞穴，那么她为什么不去洞穴里把它们抓出来呢？她完全可以召集一小队人，然后去把它们找出来。 你才不会去村里抓那只狐狸呢， [pc.name]嗯，”她回答道，微微转头望向自己小屋敞开的门外。“有好多……有好多，呃……”她结结巴巴地说着，一边用手部比划着，试图想出接下来该说什么。“尝试去抓它们并不明智。村子里有很多狼，洞穴里也可能藏着很多猎物。” 凯拉尼侧身倚在一堆草和稻草上，用手部臂支撑着自己，与你交谈。“没有其他狼会跟我一起去的。我是最棒的。 暴食症 在村子里， [pc.name]猎物被吃后的骨头就放在洞穴的前面，就像……就像，啊，就是那样。 bimlowhtre不要进来，”那些骨头说道。没有其他选择。 暴食症 拥有这个能力——或者有这个勇气——去尝试吧，因为我一个人是无法做到的。” 值得一提的是：根据凯拉尼的说法，山洞里有一些生物，她想要抓住它们，但这些生物太聪明了，会在她设置陷阱的时候躲在洞穴里不出来；而她独自去洞穴捕捉它们又太危险了。 这一点值得牢记。 稍微换个话题，你询问凯拉妮，她的狩猎进展如何。不仅仅是关于洞穴里那些猎物，还包括她为给村庄带来食物而进行的狩猎活动。 你可能会认为，在这样一个荒凉的地区，野味应该不会那么容易找到。 “我为了获取食物不得不走很远的路去狩猎，”她说道，“而且我所猎取的不仅仅是大型野兽，湖里也有大量的鱼。 我还是会打猎、也会钓鱼。” 但随后，她的表情变得阴沉起来，她的目光投向自己小屋的门。具体来说，她的视线向上移，看向挂在那里的弓——那把弓很旧，已经破旧不堪，弓弦也磨损严重，看起来下次拉弓的时候很可能会断裂。 狩猎开始了…… 太 太好了，”她说道，声音因不安而有些颤抖，“这个世界……已经不一样了。 奥姆利纳沃大块肉啊，可不要往这边来。 伊布利莫 过去人们总是去追求那些高层次的东西，但是……现在情况已经不同了。现在是他们主动来找我们。世界已经变了，而且……嗯，总之就是不一样了。 hawneio 是……”她继续用手部比划着，脸上露出困惑的表情，结结巴巴地念着那些单词。“那些…… hawneio 是 fwricht他们对这种变化并不认同。” 你以为自己能够理解她所说的“世界正在发生变化”是什么意思吧。由于最近发生的一些事件，妖怪和恶魔的数量一直在增加，这会破坏当地的动物生态系统，迫使这些动物离开它们的栖息地，从而迫使它们来到像凯拉尼和她的村庄这样的地方。你问她，村里的猎人们是否难以应对突然增多的动物数量。 凯拉尼困惑地歪了歪头，她头上的所有毛发都随着这个动作一起晃动起来。 我不明白你的意思。” 比如说，是不是动物的数量太多了，他们根本来不及捕猎……？或者这个游戏会不会对他们所在的村庄造成干扰？ 作为回应，她把头歪得更厉害了，还眯起了眼睛。 我本来是说这次狩猎活动是……”她刚开口，突然挺直身子，眼睛瞪得大大的，“哦！现在我明白你的意思了。 ibulimo 大家都很好。对我们来说，也没有对村庄构成任何威胁。但是……” 她用左手部指了指旁边一个架子，上面覆盖着一块鞣制过的皮革，看起来还很新鲜。“肉太多了……实在太多了。 umlifch骨头太多了。这次狩猎的目的并不是为了杀戮。 [pc.name]狩猎就是为了获取食物。”她再次悲伤地望着门上方那把已经破旧的弓。 奥姆利纳沃 它们就在这里，数量实在太多了。如果我们不进行捕猎，它们就会吃掉太多的草料。它们会……呃，会毁掉我们的家园，还会威胁到我们的村庄。但如果我们捕猎过度，肉就会变质，等到下一个寒冷的季节，我们就再也没有足够的肉了。我们也不能什么都不做，因为那样只会让情况变得更糟。 她叹了口气，用手部托着下巴，目光似乎飘向了远方。“我们总得做点什么……但该做什么却很难决定。[pc.isDK | 你直接问她，为什么她和其他猎人不去猎杀那些给人们带来麻烦的小妖精和恶魔。以她的能力，至少应该很容易就能对付那些小妖精吧。 “狩猎的目的并不是为了杀戮…… [pc.name]就是这个，”她重复道，“狩猎就是为了获取食物。” 其实有一个解决办法…… 那个 也是，但是…… 好吧，你想不出什么办法了。 ]

That the trap was near the caves was... not good: it is too close to where it rests. I do not know if there is more than one prey." It sounds like she's put a lot of thought into where she puts the trap, and why. Either that, or choosing where to put her traps is like second nature to her now. What more can she tell you about what it is she's hunting? "Two legs," she responds, lifting her left hand out, palm-up, and using her right hand's index and middle fingers to walk across it. "Big. More than me[pc.heightRange 0 96 |. More than you |. Might be more than you ]. But..." She twists her mouth and looks away from you, her expression a mix of frustration and embarrassment. "I have not seen it. I have seen its tracks. It lives in the caves; I am sure of that. But it does not come out while I wait." If she's so sure that something lives in those caves, but she's never seen it go in or come out, then why doesn't she go into the caves to hunt it? She could get a small team together and track it down. "You would not go in the village and hunt a vulp, [pc.name]," she responds, turning her head a bit to look out of the open door to her hut. "There are lots of... there are lots of, uhh," she stutters, gesticulating with her hands as she tries to think of the next word in her sentence. "It would not be good to try. There are lots of vulps in the village. There could be many preys in the caves." Kailani leans to one side, resting on her arm as she leans on the pile of grass and straw to talk with you. "No other vulp will join me. I am the best ibulim in the village, [pc.name]; the bones of the prey's meals lie in front of the caves, as a... as a, ah, a bimlowhtre. 'Do not come in,' the bones say. No other ibulim has the skill – or the guts – to try, and I can not do it alone." That's all interesting to note: according to Kailani, there's something living in the caves of the mountains, and she wants to hunt it down, but it's too smart to come out of the caves while she has traps set up, and going in to hunt it proactively is too dangerous by herself. That's worth keeping in mind. Shifting topics slightly, you ask Kailani how the hunt has been going in general. Not just with whatever prey is in the caves, but the hunt that she does to bring food into the village. You'd have thought that wild game wouldn't be so easy to find in an area as desolate as this. "I go far to hunt my food," she notes. "And the hunt is more than big game. Fish is – uh, there are lots of fish in the lake. I hunt and I fish all the same." But then, her expression clouds over as she looks to the door to her hut. Specifically, her eyes draw upward, toward the bow she has on display: it's old, badly worn, and the string is tattered, looking like it might snap the next time she goes to draw it. "The hunt is too good," she notes, her voice wavering with uneasiness. "The world is... not the same. Omlinawo, or, big meat, do not come this way. Ibulimo go to big meat, but... this has not been true any more. They come to us. The world is not the same and it is... um, the hawneio are..." She gesticulates with her hands some more, her face scrunching up as she stutters through her syllables. "The hawneio are fwricht. They are not well with this change." You think you can understand what she means by 'the world is changing.' Thanks to recent events, the imp and demon populations have been on the rise, which would upset the local animal ecosystems and drive them out of their habitats, forcing them towards people like Kailani and her village.You ask her if the hunters of the village are having a hard time keeping up with the sudden rush of animals. Kailani tilts her head in confusion; all of the fur and hair on her head sways and bobs with the motion. "I do not know what you mean." Like, is there too many animals for them to hunt...? Is there a risk of the game becoming intrusive to their village? She, in response, tilts her head further and squints her eyes. "I had said that the hunt is–" she starts, then her head straightens and her eyes go wide. "Oh! I see what you mean now. The ibulimo are well. There is no threat to us or to the village. But..." With her left hand, she points to a nearby rack with a tanned leather draped over it. It looks fresh. "There is too much meat. There is too much umlifch. There are too much bones. The hunt is not to kill, [pc.name]; the hunt is to eat." Again, she looks sadly at her worn bow above her door. "The omlinawo are here, and they are too much. If we do not hunt, they will graze too much. They will... uh, they will wreck our home. They could hurt our village. But if we hunt too much, meat will rot. There will too few for the next cold. We can not leave; that would make it worse." She sighs and rests her chin on the back of her hand. She looks towards you, but her gaze is a million miles away. "We can not do no thing... but it is hard to do some thing."[pc.isDK | You ask her, point-blank, why she and the other hunters don't hunt the imps and demons that are making things difficult. With skills like hers, at the very least, the imps ought to be easy to deal with. "The hunt is not to kill, [pc.name]," she repeats. "The hunt is to eat." There's a solution to that as well, but... Well, you're out of ideas. ]'

rows.original: Kailani provides for the village as one of its huntresses, and you encountering one of her traps is how you two met. Ask her about her work.
rows.translation: 作为村里的猎手之一，凯拉妮为村庄做出了贡献，而你正是遇到了她设置的陷阱，才与她相识的。不妨去问问她关于她的工作吧。
rows.raw: "Kailani provides for the village as one of its huntresses, and you encountering one of her traps is how you two met. Ask her about her work."

rows.original: You ask Kailani if she has any blood-related family among the village. Her fur color isn't unusual for a vulperine, but her hut seems somewhat small for a family to be living in. Kailani's demeanor changes drastically at the question. Where she once sat and regarded you with rapt, undivided attention, her eyes suddenly drift away and the slight smile on her face evaporates completely. Her eyes appear to glass over as she considers how to answer you – if she even has a thought going on in her head at all. She opens her mouth to answer, taking in a deep breath through it, then shuts her mouth and reconsiders. Her gaze drifts to her left suddenly and lingers there for a long while with you sitting in uncomfortable silence. [pc.isBimbo |You repeat the question, just in case. You drift off like that sometimes too, and you could use a refresher to answer. |You follow her gaze; she's looking at her staff, propped up beside the interior rock walls of her hut. The thought of changing your question to something maybe a little more comfortable for her crosses your mind... but she opens her mouth again. ] "Not by blood," she eventually answers solemnly. "No... uhh... no wilmowo?" she asks. You stare at her blankly. "No... other vulps born with me." Oh, she's saying she doesn't have any siblings. "My umwricht was a village ibulim. Many village ibulimo from my umwricht side. Big game; small game; fish. Hunt all meat. Many old hides in the village are from hunts he made." Again, she stares at the spear propped against the stone wall for a long moment. "Once," she continues, chewing through the word, "he went out to hunt. He did not come home. Vulps went to – heh, to hunt the one who hunts. Hunt and bring him home." She smirks wryly at her own joke, but it fades just as quickly as it comes up. "They find his trail, but it stops. Ib oo nah nim lambruwlechin. They could not find him. He was gone." She leans backward, her index finger twirling around a lock of her scraggly hair. She's not comfortable with sitting still. "My umfracht was not a village ibulim. But when my umwricht lambruwlechin, she was a village ibulim. She took care of kits. The most she had gone to hunt was fruit from trees." After Kailani's father disappeared, her mother jumped foot-first into the occupation, despite having no experience? "She was on the hunt for my umwricht. She thought the village ibulimo could not find him, but she could." Kailani rubs at the back of her right hand. "My umwricht left when it was warm. She did not last more than that. One day, she went out to hunt, and she did not come back. Vulps searched for days for them." [pc.isDK |You say nothing. Even if you were the type to have a warmer heart than you do, there's nothing to say. |You offer your condolences. What she's been through is something tragic that you wouldn't wish on anyone. For both of her parents to disappear like that... it would devastate anyone. ] "I was young," she continued. "It has been a long time. I know they will not come back. But I am still Ibulim Kailani. My umwricht taught me to hunt. The hawneio took me; when it was time for me to hunt, I became ibulim. One that hunts." She smiles, but it's not wide enough to show you her teeth or bright enough to reach her eyes. "The best in the village." You note, with some tepid caution, that she keeps glancing towards the spear she has leaning against the wall. Is it related to her story somehow? She looks at the spear again, this time with a more focused, discerned eye, looking over every bend of the brown, yellow, and green leathers wrapped around it. "The spear is... plain," she answers, struggling for a moment to find the right word. "The tip is plain. The wood is plain." She points to the spear, but not to any specific part of it. "The straps are not plain. They are made by an Ibulim – one in the home. I made these ones." As she speaks, the corners of her lips curl upward as she takes pride in her handiwork. "I hunt; skin the hunt; tan the hide; druunin the hide; and wrap it to the spear. The dyes are Ibulim home shades. The village knows that this is my spear." She sits back into her pile of grass and straw, relaxing her hand. "My umwricht and umfracht would have used spears with the same shades. In this way, they are with me." In that case, you turn around and point to the bow that's been hung up over the door to the hut. Its wood is naked; why doesn't it have any colored leathers on it? "It is not for the hunt," she frowns. "It was, but not now. It will break soon. I do not use it to hunt; I keep it... so that I can keep it." You suppose that's a fair enough answer. In an attempt to change the topic, you ask if she has a mate. Kailani crinkles her nose slightly at the question. "No," she answers plainly. "I... I will not take a mate until I find my umwricht and umfracht. Change is in the world, [pc.name]. The hunt is not like how it was. It is not safe to work on the hunt; there is a thing out there that took those close to me. I can not start a home while it is not safe for the Ibulim home. I will not take a mate and I will not have a child while it is not safe." So, Kailani intends to stay single and without a family until she's solved the mystery of whatever happened to her parents. She could be right: whatever's out there that got them might be targeting her family specifically, and starting a family could be dangerous, and not just for herself. Does she have any idea what happened to them? Two hunting parties couldn't find them; is she doing any better? In response, she sighs with a combination of dejection and frustration. "Yes, and no," she eventually responds. "The prey in the caves that we met near – the trails of both my umwricht and umfracht were lost near there. It has been years. I do not know that they are in those caves, but..." She leans forward, her eyes staring directly into yours and her hand over her chest. "I know they are there. Or, they were there. It is in those caves I will find them." Her voice comes out of her mouth wavy and uncertain: from the look on her face and the way she holds her stern posture, she believes that she's right – but she might not want to be. She said herself that she doesn't think that they're still alive, but if she goes into those caves, she'll at least get the answers she's looking for. Whether she wants them or not.
rows.translation: 你询问凯拉尼，她的村庄里是否有与血液相关的亲属。对于一只狐族来说，她的毛色并不罕见，但她的小屋对于一个家庭来说似乎有点太小了。 听到这个问题，凯拉尼的神情发生了巨大的变化。 曾经，她坐在那里，全神贯注地注视着你，她的目光无比专注；然而现在，她的视线突然移开了，脸上那丝淡淡的微笑也彻底消失了。她的目光似乎变得呆滞起来，似乎在思考该如何回答你——或者说，她脑子里到底在想些什么。 她张开嘴想要回答，深吸了一口气，却又闭上嘴重新考虑起来。她的目光突然转向左边，在那里停留了很长时间，使得你们陷入了尴尬的沉默之中。 [pc.isBimbo |你把问题重复一遍，以防万一。有时候你也会走神，这时再听一遍问题就能帮助你回答了。 |你顺着她的视线望去，她正看着自己那根靠在小屋内墙边的手杖。你突然想到，或许可以换个问题来问她，这样可能会让她感到更自在一些……但她却再次开口说话了。 ] 并非血缘关系，”她最终严肃地回答道，“不……呃……不是这样的。 威尔莫沃？”她问道。你茫然地望着她。“没有……和我一起出生的其他狼崽。” 哦，她是说她没有兄弟姐妹。 “我的…… 嗯……这个名称听起来有点特别吧。 那是一个村庄。 暴食症许多村庄 ibulimo 来自我的 嗯……这个名称听起来有点特别。 大型猎物、小型猎物，还有鱼……他什么都猎。村里那些古老的皮毛，很多都是他打猎得来的。” 她再次盯着靠在石墙上的那支长矛，凝视了许久。“有一次，”她继续说道，一字一顿地咀嚼着这些词语，“他出去打猎了，却再也没有回来。那些狐狸……呵呵，去猎杀那个猎人的了。去把他的尸体抓回来吧。”她自嘲地笑了笑，但这个笑话刚出现，又立刻消失了。“他们找到了他的踪迹，但线索在那里就断了。 伊布·奥·纳·尼姆·兰布鲁莱钦他们找不到他，他已经不见了。” 她向后仰靠在椅背上，用食指拨弄着自己那一绺凌乱的头发。她坐着一动不动的话，会感到很不自在。“我的…… 运费 那并不是一个村庄。 暴食症但是，当我的…… umwricht lambruwlechin她曾经是一个村庄的一员。 暴食症她负责照料那些小动物。她最多也就是去树上摘些水果而已。 在凯拉尼的父亲失踪后，她的母亲尽管没有任何经验，还是立刻投身到了工作中。 “她是在为我寻找…… 嗯……这个名称听起来有点特别吧。她认为这个村庄…… ibulimo 找不到他，但是她找到了。”凯拉妮揉了揉自己的右手背。“我的…… 嗯……这个名称听起来有点特别吧。 在天气还暖和的时候，它就离开了。它没能活过那个冬天。有一天，它出去觅食，再也没有回来。其他的狼群搜寻了它好几天，却始终找不到它的踪迹。 [pc.isDK |你什么也没说。即使你是一个内心更温暖的人，现在也实在没有什么话可说。 |您表达了深切的慰问。她所经历的一切实在是一场悲剧，没有人会希望自己遭遇这种事情。她的父母就这样离世了……这样的打击对任何人来说都将是毁灭性的。 ] 我当时还很年轻，”她继续说道，“已经过去很久了。我知道他们再也不会回来了。但我依然是伊布利姆·凯拉尼…… 嗯……这个名称听起来有点特别吧。 是它教会了我如何狩猎。 hawneio 这让我陷入了困境；每当我该去狩猎的时候，我就陷入了这种状态。 暴食症一个擅长狩猎的人。”她微笑着，但笑容并不深，既没有露出牙齿，也没有让眼睛显得明亮起来。“村里最出色的狩猎者。” 你带着几分谨慎，注意到她不时瞥向靠在墙上的那支长矛。 这和她的故事有什么关联吗？ 她再次注视着那支长矛，这一次，她的目光更加专注、更加细致，仔细观察着包裹在长矛上的那些棕色、黄色和绿色的皮革所形成的每一处褶皱。“这支长矛，确实和她的故事有关。很普通，”她回答道，一时找不到合适的词语来形容。“矛头很普通，木材也很普通。”她指了指那支矛，但并没有指出它的任何具体部位。“不过编织矛柄的带子却很不普通——它们是由家里的伊布利姆制作的。 这些都是我亲手制作的。”她边说边嘴角上扬，为自己的手艺感到自豪。“我会去捕猎，然后将猎物剥皮，再将皮革晒成棕褐色…… 德鲁宁 把皮剥下来，然后把它包在长矛上。这些染料是伊布利姆家乡特有的颜色。全村的人都知道这是…… 我的 长矛。” 她重新坐回那堆草和稻草上，放松了自己的手。“我的…… 嗯……这个名称听起来有点特别吧。 以及 运费 我本来也会使用那些颜色相同的长矛。这样，它们就能和我一起战斗了。” 于是，你转过身去，指向挂在小屋门上的那把弓。它的木制部分没有经过任何装饰；为什么没有覆盖上任何彩色的皮革呢？ 它并不是用来打猎的，”她皱着眉头说，“以前是用来打猎的，但现在不是了。它很快就会坏掉。我并不是用它来打猎的；我留着它……只是因为我想把它留下来。” 你认为这个回答已经很合理了。为了改变话题，你便问她是否有伴侣。 听到这个问题，凯拉妮微微皱了皱鼻子，然后干脆地回答道：“不会。在我找到属于我的那个人之前，我……我不会选择伴侣的。 嗯……这个名称听起来有点特别吧。 以及 运费世界在变化， [pc.name]现在的狩猎已经和过去不一样了。在这种环境下进行狩猎根本不安全，因为有一种未知的威胁已经夺走了我身边的一些人。在Ibulim的家园还不安全的情况下，我无法开始建立新的家庭。在这种危险的环境中，我既不会寻找伴侣，也不会生育孩子。所以，凯拉尼决定保持单身，不组建家庭，直到她弄清楚父母身上究竟发生了什么。她的想法可能是正确的：那些导致他们遭遇不幸的势力，可能专门在针对她的家人，而组建家庭可能会带来危险，而且这种危险不仅会威胁到她自己。 她知道他们发生了什么事吗？两个搜救队都找不到他们，她有没有找到任何线索呢？ 作为回应，她叹了口气，语气中充满了沮丧与无奈。“嗯，也算知道吧，又算不知道……”她最终这样回答道。 我们在附近洞穴里遇到的那些猎物——还有我的那些痕迹…… 嗯……这个名称听起来有点特别吧。 以及 运费 他们在那附近失踪了。已经过去很多年了。我不知道他们是否还在那些洞穴里，但是……”她向前倾了倾身子，目光直视着你的眼睛，双手放在胸前，“我…… 知道 他们就在那里。或者说，他们曾经在那里。我一定会在那些洞穴里找到他们。 她的声音听起来有些颤抖，显得有些不确定：从她脸上的表情以及她那坚定的姿态来看，她似乎坚信自己是正确的——但也许她并不真的这么认为。她自己也曾说过，她不认为他们还活着，但只要她走进那些洞穴，至少就能得到她一直在寻找的答案。 无论她是否真的想要那些答案。

I will not take a mate and I will not have a child while it is not safe." So, Kailani intends to stay single and without a family until she's solved the mystery of whatever happened to her parents. She could be right: whatever's out there that got them might be targeting her family specifically, and starting a family could be dangerous, and not just for herself. Does she have any idea what happened to them? Two hunting parties couldn't find them; is she doing any better? In response, she sighs with a combination of dejection and frustration. "Yes, and no," she eventually responds. "The prey in the caves that we met near – the trails of both my umwricht and umfracht were lost near there. It has been years. I do not know that they are in those caves, but..." She leans forward, her eyes staring directly into yours and her hand over her chest. "I know they are there. Or, they were there. It is in those caves I will find them." Her voice comes out of her mouth wavy and uncertain: from the look on her face and the way she holds her stern posture, she believes that she's right – but she might not want to be. She said herself that she doesn't think that they're still alive, but if she goes into those caves, she'll at least get the answers she's looking for. Whether she wants them or not.'
