rows.original: [var0 |You ask Kailani if it's alright for you and Inaya to join her on a hunting trip, maybe to help bring the kills back or something. Inaya hasn't decided what it is she wants to be when she grows up yet, but surely Kailani would prefer it if she joined her mother in hunting to provide for the village. Kailani, however, frowns at the suggestion. She places a hand on your shoulder to turn you around so that you're both facing away from Inaya, and once you do, she leans into you and lowers her voice to a whisper. "It is true that I would like Inaya to hunt," she answers, "but she is too young. The, uh... the flaarumliumo of the hunt is no thing for a child. I was... not as young when I made my first kill." You ask her what her first kill was. "A pig, tied to a post," she answers. "Born to be food. It was not a clean kill. The sound and the blood were..." She trails off for a moment, her eyes focusing on something in the distance before snapping back to you. "I hope to spare Inaya the... acts that I made. And even then!" she continues, straightening her back and speaking with a higher volume, clearly wanting Inaya to hear what she has to say next. "The hunt is done with ibulimo. Too many on the hunt will make it too hard. The noise; the tracks. When I hunt with vulps, it is with no more than three, and all three are the best at what we do." Maybe she's right, and it's a little too early to take Inaya out actually hunting. If Kailani were 'on the job' and she was really trying to hunt an animal to bring back for food and skinning, you and Inaya would just slow her down. But is there anything else you three could do? Inaya could use some direction and a good head-start on her training. Kailani crosses her arms and thinks. Her eyes trail along the outside foundation of her hut as she considers the question – and, eventually, a light, coy smile starts to spread across her face. "I can think on one thing," she answers. |Inaya really seemed to enjoy spending time with you and Kailani the last time you three went out to train her in how to hunt, and honestly, you think you learned a thing or two yourself. You ask Kailani if there are any other lessons she could teach you both: on top of her being a good teacher, it's a[pc.isDK |n acceptable | wonderful ] bonding experience for you three. "Ah, yes," she answers, nodding her head and smiling so that you can see her pointed teeth. "I am glad you like them too, [pc.name]. And I am glad that you asked!" She tilts her head as she looks at you, her eyes narrowing affectionately. "It is good that you like to learn to hunt, too. It is a good skill to have – and I am glad to teach." ] [rand | Kailani disappears into her hut for just a moment; when she returns, in her hands are half a dozen sticks, each of them carefully whittled of their bark and their surfaces worn smooth. The sticks are worn and weathered, looking as though they've been sitting somewhere in her hut for quite some time; you notice that each of them has one end that's been worn down more than the others, as if something was attached to their flattened ends at one point. They look like they might have been bodies for spears at once point...? None of them are broken, but rather than throw any of her old and used ones out, she kept them stored, maybe for this exact situation. Being on top of a snowy, harsh mountain, good wood that can be fashioned into weapons might be hard to come by. "Come," Kailani says to both you and Inaya, nodding towards the entrance to the village. She has something in mind, but it's not to be inside the village borders, clearly. She leads you a small distance from the village – not so far that Inaya would have difficulty finding her way back, if worse came to worst. It's a widened, flattened area that looks as though it sees a fair amount of traffic on-and-off: the plateau is stamped flat with so many footprints in the snow that it's impossible to discern one from another. On the other side of the plateau is a sheer drop off that goes straight down the mountain, and it's a long way down. On the opposite side, the wall of the mountain reaches higher above you, and the stone wall is dressed with circles of different colors and shapes, drawn crudely directly onto the stone; the chalk is starting to flake and needs reapplying. Near the circles, and especially inside them, the stone of the wall is pockmarked and scratched all over, as if something had been clawing at them over and over. Finally, a pile of flatter stones has been assembled in a neat pile near the stone wall, several paces off in the distance. Kailani gives you two of the sticks, and Inaya the other three, keeping one for herself. "Okay," she says, guiding you to the center of the plateau, with your back to the chasm. Although you're in no danger of falling off the mountain, it still gives you pause, knowing that the drop-off is right there. "[pc.name], this is where vulps... learn to throw the spear." She grips her stick at the halfway point, underhanded; when she lifts it over her shoulder, she spreads her legs and leans back slightly, looking as though she's ready to throw it with all her might. "You must throw the spear and land the point in the marks. You stop when you do not miss." This is how the vulperine hunters get used to the weight of their spears and the strength of their own arms – although these training spears lack sharpened tips, meaning they're unbalanced compared to the spears tipped with metal or obsidian like you've seen Kailani use. Still, the training is good, and once Inaya is older and more confident in her skills, she can graduate to a more appropriate training weapon. You're a quick learner and find that you can be proficient with most weapons given a bit of time, but what Kailani's asking you to do is a little different from what you're used to. Kailani instructs you on how to grip the spear, and how wide your legs ought to be as you ready yourself to throw it. It's a simple posture that you take to naturally, and the motion feels good and your arm feels strong when you throw it, but your aim is constantly off and you have a hard time honing in on how much, or how little, strength you need. Kailani is teaching you a hunting stance, when you're more used to combat stances that emphasize power over accuracy, and on top of that, the wind on top of the mountain alternates between calm and fierce, constantly forcing you to readjust yourself when you think you have it right. Inaya doesn't fare a whole lot better, either: you and her stand the same distance away from the wall, and she needs to put more muscle into throwing the spear than you do, often to worse results. She has a harder time getting back into a proper throwing stance, and when she throws the spear, she either puts too much focus on accuracy and form, or not enough. Still, though, she's having a blast with trying, and you and her make a game out of how many spears you can get into the targets. Green circles are worth one point, while yellow circles, typically higher on the wall, are worth two. She laughs and cheers whenever she gets a point and she gets focused and intense whenever you get one, but really, neither of you are keeping track of how many points you have: what's more important is the time you three are spending together. And even then, the emphasis on scoring points is teaching her body positive habits – the more often she scores, the more often she tries to replicate what worked, and that's going to start working into her muscle memory. She'll be one of the best spear-throwing hunters in the village by the time she's ready. Once Inaya consistently gets into a proper stance on her own, Kailani breaks away from you two. "One more test," she says as she makes her way to the pile of flat rocks stacked neatly on top of each other at the base of the wall. She picks one up, showing you both the flattened side – and scrawled onto its granite is a crude, flaking red circle. "The hunt will not sit still for long. A good vulp ibulim must hit a hunt that runs. Inaya, [pc.name]: try and hit this!" With that, and a flick of her wrist, Kailani tosses the rock lengthwise across the cliff's face, letting it spin through the air with the red circle facing towards you. Neither you nor Inaya were ready for it, and neither of you throw your spear at it. You've already failed: if this were a real hunt, your quarry would have gotten away. There are more rocks in the pile next to Kailani, though, and with another flick, she tosses another flat rock, giving you both a moving target to try and hit. Inaya swings first, and you second, but neither of you land the hit. And to make things harder, Kailani keeps mixing up the angle of her toss, and how quickly they travel: sometimes they go high with a steep arc, and sometimes they're quick and lower to the ground. The constant winds interrupting all three of you don't make things any easier, either. Kailani runs out of rocks to throw before either of you score a hit, but rather than call the practice over, she simply goes to the other side of the plateau, where all the rocks she just threw are, and starts again, tossing them back to the other side. Inaya has three spears while you only have two, giving her an unfair advantage, but it honestly doesn't matter: if she manages to land a strike before you do, it's not because she had one more spear to toss than you did. On one particular toss, [rand |Inaya throws her spear – and the familiar sound of battered, old, flattened wood cracking against stone midair echoes over the plateau, causing the stone disk to wobble and alter its course as it falls to the ground. Inaya had gotten the strike! After a quick celebratory dance, you both agree that that particular hit was worth a million points, and the game is over. |you throw your spear – and the familiar sound of battered, old, flattened wood cracking against stone midair echoes over the plateau, causing the stone disk to wobble and alter its course as it falls to the ground. You managed to get the strike first! But since neither of you agreed on how many points the red circles were worth beforehand, Inaya insists that it's only worth one, meaning that she probably still won the game between you two. ] You help Kailani pick up and stack the rocks one more time for the next group of vulperine hunters that come by. The poor, naked spears will definitely need replacing soon... but in the meantime, that wasn't half-bad practice in teaching Inaya how to hold, aim, and throw a spear. She's one step closer to being a hunter worthy of the name 'ibulim'. | Kailani bids that you follow her. You and Inaya do so as she leads you towards the village's fletcher: a hunter, by the looks of the vulperine at the hut, who's retired and spends their time making hunting weapons and apparel instead. After exchanging a few words (and the retired vulperine gives you a look that you can't immediately discern), the fletcher gives Kailani two bows, as well as some practice arrows: arrow shafts with proper fletchings, but no tips, so that the shafts just end in a dull point. It'd hurt like hell to get shot by them, but it'd be very unlikely to do any permanent damage, even from a trained, practiced archer. The bows themselves look to be proper and well-maintained, although one of them is much too small for you and the string appears stretchier than it ought to be to get any real thrusting power. "Come," Kailani says to both you and Inaya, nodding towards the entrance to the village. She has something in mind, but it's not to be inside the village borders, clearly. She leads you a small distance from the village – not so far that Inaya would have difficulty finding her way back, if worse came to worst. It's a widened, flattened area that looks as though it sees a fair amount of traffic on-and-off: the plateau is stamped flat with so many footprints in the snow that it's impossible to discern one from another. On the other side of the plateau is a sheer drop off that goes straight down the mountain, and it's a long way down. On the opposite side, the wall of the mountain reaches higher above you, and the stone wall is dressed with circles of different colors and shapes, drawn crudely directly onto the stone; the chalk is starting to flake and needs reapplying. Near the circles, and especially inside them, the stone of the wall is pockmarked and scratched all over, as if something had been clawing at them over and over. Finally, a pile of flatter stones has been assembled in a neat pile near the stone wall, several paces off in the distance. Kailani gives Inaya the smaller bow [var1 |and keeps the larger bow for herself, seeing as you already have one ready. She doles out the practice arrows, giving you and Inaya four each while saving the last two for herself |and gives you the other – it's much larger and better suited to your frame. She doles out the practice arrows, giving you and Inaya five each ]. "Okay," she says, guiding you to the center of the plateau, with your back to the chasm. Although you're in no danger of falling off the mountain, it still gives you pause, knowing that the drop-off is right there. "We learn how to use a bow. [pc.name], you and Inaya must shoot the... the rrumba," she says, rolling the R as she lifts the practice arrow for emphasis, "at the marks. You stop when you do not miss." This is where vulperine hunters go to get used to practice their archery: everything from accuracy to the draw strength in their arms and the strength required to shoot their bows. Although the practice arrows have no tips (and aren't as aerodynamic as a real thing), they're nonetheless a good starting point for a new hunter to get used to how to properly nock an arrow. Once a new recruit gets used to that, they can get started on learning how a proper arrow flies – it'd be dangerous for an archer that didn't know how to prepare an arrow before firing to use real equipment. You're [var1 |already proficient with bows, and you're comfortable enough with your own that firing arrows is like second nature. Most of your shots fire true on the targets – although, you stick with the practice arrows, and there are some growing pains with getting used to how they fly. You can tell from Kailani's own accuracy that she's the exact same way: able to nock and fire them without issue, but her aim is ever-so-slightly off and needs occasional readjustment to hit her targets. |proficient with a variety of weapons, and although you don't typically use a bow, you're a quick learner and take to nocking and firing the arrow expertly after only a few attempts. Your accuracy, however, leaves something else to be desired, particularly since the arrow doesn't quite fly the way you expect it to, given its shape. You can tell that Kailani has some of the same issues: able to prepare and launch the arrow well enough, but her accuracy is ever-so-slightly off with every launch and needs constant fine-tuning. That, and she typically hunts with a spear: her practice with a bow might be a little rusty. ] Inaya, however, struggles quite a bit with her bow. The drawstring requires more strength than she's ready to give it, and she has a hard time nocking the arrow into place: when she gets it upright, it falls out of place, and the few times she does manage to fire it, it flies off in an unpredictable angle, and often sideways (prompting you and Kailani to give her a wider berth than usual). When she manages to pull the drawstring back, her arms shake unsteadily, further throwing off her aim. She holds her breath while taking aim – which is proper form – but she holds it as she's drawing the string, and she holds it for too long, causing her to gasp from exhaustion and release the arrow too soon once more. Kailani is a patient teacher, though. You don't understand most of the words she uses to instruct her daughter, but given her tone, she probably had just as much trouble holding a bow and arrow when she was Inaya's age. Her hands help Inaya set the arrow into place and help her hold the bow up properly; she teaches Inaya that her bow arm needs to be locked straight, and to not bring the fletching of the arrow right up against her eyes. Eventually, after many, many failed starts, Inaya brings the arrow into place; she nocks it properly; she pulls the drawstring back; she closes one eye; she holds her breath as she takes aim; and she lets go. And the arrow flies... mostly straight. It doesn't hit any of the targets, but the bow makes a satisfying 'fwip!' sound as it goes, the bowstring twangs into place, and the arrow, unlike every other arrow Inaya had 'fired' up until this point, hits the rocky surface of the wall with a sturdy, solid impact. "Yay!" Inaya cheers, jumping up and down high enough to bend her knees. She quickly runs over to the arrow she just fired, picking it up and showing it first to Kailani, then to you, in her excitement. The blunted, featureless tip of the shaft is even a bit frayed and splintered from the impact – it was a powerful hit that would have easily pierced the hide of any animal on the mountain, if it was properly tipped. Despite all the practice she's getting, and all the instruction from the best hunter in her village, Inaya's 'successful' shots are few and far between... which makes all the good shots worth celebrating over like she is now. Inaya moves to nock the arrow and try again, but Kailani stops her, putting her hand on the bow's raised edge and lowering it back down. "Wayto ko gillum." She looks to you (and needs to raise her voice a little over the howling winds of the mountain). "We are done for now." Inaya pouts and lowers her bow, holding it lengthwise across her lap – and you can immediately see why Kailani called it off: the fur around the underside of Inaya's left wrist is starting to wear thin. A few more incorrect shots, and the natural bracers of her fur will be torn away, and that'd probably hurt more than the drawstring hitting her wrist by itself. In fact, you're surprised that it isn't bothering Inaya more than she's letting it on. But then again, maybe she's just tough like her mom that way. | "Come," Kailani says to both you and Inaya, nodding towards the entrance to the village. She has something in mind, but it's not to be inside the village borders, clearly. She leads you a fair distance away from the village, well beyond eyesight of its borders, although not off the beaten trail surrounding the mountaintop. The path leading away from the village is twisting and winding, and at times it's thin and precarious, especially with the higher winds – but both Kailani and Inaya walk as though it's not anything difficult or even unusual. Despite their fluffy fur producing so much more drag, they've gotten so used to the conditions in the mountain that even the high winds don't knock them off balance or cause their feet to misstep. You need help walking the path more often than [pc.isDK |a literal child does |either of them do ]. Eventually, Kailani leads you to a large clearing, covered in snow – wait, no, it's not a field: it's a lake. A frozen lake, the ice sturdy enough to support your weight, even fully-geared as you are. Chunks of the lake's icy top has been cut and lifted away, revealing the calm-but-treacherous water underneath. Torn and discarded offal line the banks of the lake, where there's evidence of past temporary shelters having been established. With both of these facts together, you guess that ice fishing is a common method of providing food for the vulperine village. But Kailani doesn't lead you onto the icy surface of the lake (something you breathe a sigh of relief over). Instead, she leads you to one of the lakes several streams feeding into the lake: the water continues to run despite the chill in the air, preventing it from freezing, and the mouths of the streams feeding into the lake go for a small distance before disappearing underneath the icecap. "Fish is an easy hunt," Kailani says – as she steps directly into the running water, barefoot. The thick fur surrounding her feet must give her much, much better insulation than you thought. Or maybe she's just tough as nails. "We can not feed all vulps in the village with just fish. But fish can feed one vulp. It can feed two." She looks to you and smiles, her deep blue eyes vanishing slightly beneath her eyes as her cheeks lift up. "And one mate." Inaya, undaunted and confident, steps into the running stream water with her mother, ready to fish alongside her. [pc.ra vulperine |Despite being vulperine yourself, you're not native to the boreal region and the cold still bites into you; you pass on stepping into frigid water this time. |[pc.hasSkinTags furred |Despite being covered in fur, you |You don't have the advantage of being covered in fur, and you ] aren't native to the frigid, boreal region; you pass on stepping into frigid water and exposing your toes to those kinds of conditions this time. ] You'll just have to watch from the sidelines this time. Swimming through the water and visibly around Kailani's and Inaya's feet are fish: simple, un-exotic trout whose scales gleam underneath the sparkle of the sun reflecting against the water. There's only maybe four of them, and they dart away every time either Kailani or Inaya take a step, but they're quick to reform around their feet, swimming up against the current. "Siln gaus," she whispers to Inaya, patting her on the head gently, as if trying to fine-tune Inaya's stance and position. "Darlum gurd ki fil." Following whatever instruction Kailani gave her, Inaya stays perfectly still in the water: her knees slightly bent with her hands up, palms pointed towards to streaming water. Her tail is up slightly, trying to keep it from falling into the running water, although you can see the strain and effort she's putting in to keep it steady – all of that fur on her tail is awfully heavy. Kailani is just as still and quiet, but she's much more practiced, with her muscles, including her tail, truly kept stock-still as she stands in the water. Both of their stances are wide, with their knees just slightly bent, giving them greater stability against the rushing currents and lowering their bodies just a little bit, bringing them closer to the water. The trout around their ankles start to get complacent, forgetting that two large vulperines had just stepped into their water. Their tail-fins swim and swish through the current, trying to push themselves forward and around their feet – and as soon as one of them gets just a little too close, Kailani whips her hand into the water, her fingers all straightened out so that they slice into the surface rather than batter or slap against it. Just as quickly as it happens, she pulls it out, and in her hand is a wriggling, flopping, slippery fish, desperately trying to break free from her grip and get back into the water she had just yanked it from. The whole action, from start to finish, took maybe as long as it takes for you to blink. "Whoa," Inaya gasps, her eyes going wide at the sight of her mother catching a fish straight out of the stream like that. She lets herself relax enough that her tail dips into the water, causing her to yip and jump in surprise at the sudden chill, something she wasn't prepared for, and that causes all of the fish around her ankles to scatter. Kailani laughs well-meaningly as she gently lowers the panic-stricken fish back into the stream of water, letting it go. It immediately darts back into the lake behind her... although you wouldn't be surprised if it comes right back in a minute. "Like that," she says to Inaya, but her eyes flit up to you to check that you're paying attention. Just in case you ever need to catch a fish straight out of the water with your hands. "Atislin. Aflit. Faelwa yol inglam tag vie." She stands back up and pats Inaya on the head once more. "Try." Inaya's body goes rigid, her tail upright along the stream of the water. She keeps herself as still as can be: everything from not moving a muscle to holding her breath, barely daring to move her eyes along the water's surface to track the fish around her feet. She pauses, trying to get a good bead on one of the trout swimming around her ankles, and she ever-so-slightly starts to lower her body to try and give herself a head-start on catching the fish around herself. That, unfortunately, causes the muscles around her ankles to flex, followed by her calves, and the trout around her legs recognize the minute changes in the water's tension. They don't dart away, but they start to avoid her body, swimming out of reach. If she wanted to catch one, she'd have to extend her arm and lean, which would upset her balance and might even dunk her into the water if she wasn't careful. "Stop," Kailani says sternly, and although Inaya takes her time resetting herself into an upright standing position, she obeys her mother's tone more than her word. "Siln. Gaus." "Gaus ui silntre nah!" Inaya protests in confusion, shrugging her shoulders and waving her hands as if she was trying to barter with Kailani. Whatever it was that Kailani told her to do, it sounded like she thought she was doing it, but is confused on what she's getting wrong. In response, Kailani erupts into a series of sentences, her mouth saying words faster than you can track, with her hands going everywhere from patting the width of her thighs, to the backs of her calves, before swishing her fingers along the surface of the water – and Inaya listens intently to all of it, her brow furrowed in focus as she listens to Kailani's instructions. "Igue," Inaya eventually says once Kailani's done with her teaching, nodding once in resolution before getting back into her wide stance, her knees slightly bent in the water, with her head tilted downwards to watch the trout in the stream. It takes some time before the fish start to gain the confidence to start swimming around Inaya's ankles once more, and once they do, her focus visibly tightens, although she also puts in the conscious effort to keep from moving even the littlest bit, unlike what she had done last time. Before, she bent at the waist to try and give herself a bit of extra leeway; this time, taking whatever Kailani had told her to heart, she stands perfectly, completely still, save for her eyes watching the scales of the trout gleaming underneath the water's surface. She takes a bit more time to ready herself compared to Kailani, but after a few tense moments, Inaya slaps her hand into the water like her mother had, extending her fingers so that they cut into the surface rather than splash into it. Her angle is just a little off, though, and her palm slaps into the water's surface, cutting down on her speed – when she pulls her hand out of the water, she has a fish by the tail, but her grip is weak and the fish thrashes back and forth with just enough intensity that it manages to break free from her grasp. She tries to catch it several times as it falls, but as soon as it hits the water, it's gone. "Laug!" she says in frustration as both of her hands thrust into the water to try and catch the fish, but you and Kailani both know that it's long gone. You're pretty sure Inaya knows it too, but she's trying to put off admitting it. Still, Kailani puts a reassuring hand on Inaya's shoulder, getting her to stop her thrashing in the water for a fish that's not even there anymore. "Good," she says to Inaya. "Next time." As she and Inaya wade out of the water – the droplets in their fur already starting to freeze to icicles as they go, but neither of them showing any discomfort as they walk – you ask Kailani if fish are out-of-season or something. Why did she let her catch go? Was it so there would be more to catch once the seasons change? Kailani laughs, then shakes her head, causing all of the wild hair on her head to sway as she does. "No," she answers honestly. "I just do not like the taste of fish." Oh. That's as good a reason as any. ]
rows.translation: [var0 |你询问凯拉尼，你是否可以和伊奈亚一起参加她的狩猎之旅，或许可以帮助带回猎物之类的。伊奈亚还没有决定自己长大后想成为什么，但想必凯拉尼会希望她能和母亲一起参与狩猎，为村庄做出贡献。 然而，凯拉尼对这个建议表示不满。她把手放在你的肩上，将你转向另一侧，使得你们俩都背对伊奈亚。然后她靠近你，压低声音低声说道：“我确实希望伊奈亚能去狩猎，但她还太年轻了。 那个，呃……那个…… flaarumliumo 参与狩猎根本不适合小孩子。我第一次杀死猎物时……已经不是那么年轻了。” 你问她第一次杀死的是什么猎物。 “是一头被绑在柱子上的猪，”她回答道，“它生来就是为了被吃掉的。那次猎杀并不干净利落。 那些声音，还有那些鲜血……”她停顿了片刻，目光投向远处的某个地方，随后又重新将视线转向你。“我希望自己能够避免让伊奈亚经历那些我曾经做过的事情。但即便如此……”她继续说道，挺直身子，提高了音量，显然希望伊奈亚能够听到她接下来要说的话。 狩猎已经结束。 ibulimo如果参与狩猎的人太多，就会让整个行动变得过于困难——那些噪音，还有留下的足迹……当我与那些母狼一起狩猎时，我们最多只会有三个人，而且这三个人都是我们这一行中最出色的。” 也许她说得对，现在让伊奈亚真正去参与狩猎确实还为时过早。如果凯拉妮真的在认真地狩猎，试图捕捉动物来获取食物和皮毛，你和伊奈亚只会拖慢她的进度。但你们三个人还能做些什么呢？伊奈亚确实需要帮助…… 一些 方向，以及一个良好的训练起点。 凯拉尼双臂交叉，陷入沉思。她的目光沿着自己小屋的外墙缓缓移动，一边思考着这个问题——最终，她脸上浮现出一丝羞涩而温柔的微笑。“我想出了一件事，”她回答道。 |上次你们三个人一起出去训练伊奈亚如何狩猎时，她似乎真的很享受和你以及凯拉妮在一起的时光。说实话，你觉得自己也学到了一些东西。于是你问凯拉妮，是否还有其他技巧可以教给你们俩——除了她本身就是一个出色的老师之外，她肯定还有其他值得分享的经验。[pc.isDK |不可接受 | 太棒了 ] 对你们三个人来说，这是一次增进感情的体验。 “啊，是的，”她回答道，一边点头一边微笑，让你们能看到她那整齐的牙齿。“我很高兴你们也喜欢它们。 [pc.name]我很高兴你提出了这个问题！”她歪着头看着你，眼中充满了宠溺与欣慰。“你能愿意学习狩猎，真是太好了。这是一项非常实用的技能——能够教你，我感到非常开心。 ] [rand | 凯拉尼走进小屋片刻后便回来了，她手中拿着一打木棍，每根木棍的树皮都被仔细削去，表面也被磨得光滑平整。这些木棍看起来已经使用了很长时间，仿佛在她的小屋里放了很久；你会注意到，每根木棍的一头都被磨得比其他部分更光滑，仿佛曾经有东西被固定在那些扁平的末端上。 它们看起来似乎曾经被用作长矛的柄部……？这些柄部没有一根是损坏的，而她并没有把那些旧柄部扔掉，而是把它们保存了起来，也许正是为了应对这样的情况。在积雪覆盖、环境恶劣的高山上，能够用来制作武器的优质木材恐怕很难找到。 过来吧，”凯拉尼对你们俩说道，同时指向村庄的入口。她似乎有什么打算，但显然并不是要进入村庄的内部。 在水中游动，明显围绕着凯拉妮和伊奈亚的足部游动的，是一些鱼——那些普通的、并不稀奇的鳟鱼，它们的鳞片在阳轻型的照射下闪闪发轻型。大概只有四条这样的鱼，每当凯拉妮或伊奈亚迈出一步，它们就会迅速游开，但很快又会重新聚集在她们足部边，逆流而上继续游动。西尔恩·高斯她轻声对伊奈亚说道，同时轻轻拍了拍她的头，仿佛在试图调整伊奈亚的姿势和位置。达尔伦·古尔德的剑按照凯拉妮给出的指示，伊奈亚在水中一动不动：她的膝盖微微弯曲，双手部举过头顶，手部掌朝向湍急的水流。她的尾巴也微微翘起，努力不让它被水流冲走，不过可以看出她为了保持平衡而付出了多大的努力——她尾巴上的那些毛发实在太重了。 那些在他们足部踝周围游动的鳟鱼开始变得放松警惕，完全忘记了有两条体型庞大的狐狸鱼刚刚进入了它们的水域。这些狐狸鱼的尾鳍在水中摆动着，试图让自己向前游动、绕过他们的足部边——而每当其中一条鱼靠得太近时，凯拉尼就会迅速将手部伸入水中，手部指完全伸直，这样她的手部指就能切过水面，而不会只是拍打或触碰水面。 事情发生得如此迅速，她一把抓住了它，手部中握着一条正在扭动、扑腾、滑溜溜的鱼，这条鱼拼命地想要挣脱她的控制，重新回到它刚刚被她拉出来的水中。整个过程，从开始到结束，可能只需要你眨一下眼睛那么短的时间而已。 哇哦，”伊奈亚惊呼道，看到母亲那样直接从小溪里抓到一条鱼，她的眼睛瞪得大大的。她放松下来，结果尾巴不小心浸入了水中，突如其来的寒冷让她吓得尖叫起来，连连跳跃，完全没料到会这样。 那个 这一举动使得她足部踝周围的所有鱼儿都四散逃开了。 凯拉尼善意地笑了笑，然后轻轻地将那些惊慌失措的鱼放回溪流中，让它们继续游动。那些鱼立刻又游回了她身后的湖里……不过，如果你看到它们不一会儿又游了回来，也不会感到惊讶。“就像这样，”她对伊奈亚说道，但她的目轻型却不时瞥向你，确认你正在认真观察。毕竟，总有一天你可能会需要用手部直接从水中抓鱼呢。阿蒂斯林。阿弗利特。费尔瓦，你将永远留在我的心中。她再次站起身来，轻拍了一下伊奈亚的头部：“试试看。” 伊奈亚的身体瞬间变得僵硬，尾巴也笔直地竖立在水流中。她竭力保持静止：从不动一下肌肉，到屏住呼吸，甚至不敢用眼睛沿着水面移动，去观察足部边游动的鱼儿。 她停了下来，试图瞄准那些在她的足部踝周围游动的鳟鱼，然后她微微低下身体，试图让自己更容易抓住这些鱼。 然而，不幸的是，这个动作导致她足部踝周围的肌肉开始收缩，接着是小腿也跟着紧张起来，而那些在她腿边游动的鳟鱼立刻察觉到了水中这些细微的变化。 它们并不会迅速逃开，而是开始避开她的身体，游到她够不到的地方。如果她想抓住其中一条，就必须伸长手部臂并向前倾斜，这样会打破她的平衡，如果不小心的话，甚至可能会让她掉进水中。 停下来，”凯拉尼严厉地说道。虽然伊娜雅花了一些时间才重新站直身体，但她更听从母亲的肌肉度而非话语本身。西尔恩·高斯。" "高斯用户界面，安静无声。啊！”伊奈亚困惑地抗议着，耸着肩膀、挥舞着手部臂，仿佛在试图与凯拉妮进行协商。无论凯拉妮让她做什么，听起来都像是…… 思考 她正在尝试做这件事，但却不清楚自己哪里做错了。 作为回应，凯拉妮开始急促地说话，她的嘴巴说出的话语快得让人根本跟不上节奏，而她的双手部也在不停地活动——时而轻拍自己的大腿，时而抚摸小腿后侧，还不时用手部指在水面上划动。伊奈亚则全神贯注地听着她的话，眉头紧锁，努力理解凯拉妮的指示。伊格等凯拉尼教完我之后，伊奈亚最终说道。她坚定地点了点头，然后又恢复了原来的姿势：双膝微微弯曲站在水中，头微微低垂，注视着溪流中的鳟鱼。 过了一段时间，那些鱼才终于重新获得了信心，开始在伊奈亚的足部踝周围游来游去。当它们真正开始这样做的时候，伊奈亚的注意力明显变得更加集中了。不过，与上次不同的是，她这次也刻意克制自己，不让自己的身体有一丝一毫的移动。 之前，她总是弯下腰来，试图为自己争取一些活动空间；但这一次，她把凯拉妮告诉她的那些话牢记在心，站得笔直而静止，唯有她的眼睛紧紧注视着水面上那些闪烁着轻型芒的鳟鱼鳞片。 与凯拉尼相比，她需要更多时间来做好准备，但经过几秒钟的紧张等待后，伊奈亚还是像她母亲那样将手部伸入水中，手部指伸得笔直，让水花不会四溅，而是直接划破水面。 不过，她的角度稍微有点偏差，结果她的手部掌拍在了水面上，这使得她的速度大大减慢了。当她把手部从水中抽出来时，她的手部里抓住了一条鱼的尾巴，但是抓得不够紧，那条鱼拼命地挣扎着，最终还是从她的手部中逃脱了。 它掉落的时候，她试图多次抓住它，但只要它一接触到水面，就立刻消失不见了。 "笑声啊！”她沮丧地说道，双手部同时伸入水中试图抓住那条鱼，但你和凯拉尼都清楚，那条鱼早就跑掉了。你也很确定伊娜亚也知道这一点，只是她还在试图拖延承认这个事实。 尽管如此，凯拉尼还是把手部放在伊娜亚的肩上，让她停止在水中拼命寻找早已不见的鱼。“好了，”她对伊娜亚说，“下次再试吧。” 当她们俩从水中走出来时，身上的水滴已经开始结成冰柱，但她们俩却丝毫没有感到不适。这时你便问凯拉尼，是不是现在不是捕鱼的季节之类的原因。 她为什么放开手部了呢？难道是打算等季节变换后再去捕捉更多的东西吗？ 凯拉妮笑了起来，然后摇了摇头，她那一头乱蓬蓬的头发也随之晃动起来。“不，”她诚实地回答道。 我就是不喜欢鱼的味道。” 哦，这确实是个很好的理由。 ]
rows.raw: " [var0 |You ask Kailani if it's alright for you and Inaya to join her on a hunting trip, maybe to help bring the kills back or something. Inaya hasn't decided what it is she wants to be when she grows up yet, but surely Kailani would prefer it if she joined her mother in hunting to provide for the village. Kailani, however, frowns at the suggestion. She places a hand on your shoulder to turn you around so that you're both facing away from Inaya, and once you do, she leans into you and lowers her voice to a whisper. "It is true that I would like Inaya to hunt," she answers, "but she is too young. The, uh... the flaarumliumo of the hunt is no thing for a child. I was... not as young when I made my first kill." You ask her what her first kill was. "A pig, tied to a post," she answers. "Born to be food. It was not a clean kill. The sound and the blood were..." She trails off for a moment, her eyes focusing on something in the distance before snapping back to you. "I hope to spare Inaya the... acts that I made. And even then!" she continues, straightening her back and speaking with a higher volume, clearly wanting Inaya to hear what she has to say next. "The hunt is done with ibulimo. Too many on the hunt will make it too hard. The noise; the tracks. When I hunt with vulps, it is with no more than three, and all three are the best at what we do." Maybe she's right, and it's a little too early to take Inaya out actually hunting. If Kailani were 'on the job' and she was really trying to hunt an animal to bring back for food and skinning, you and Inaya would just slow her down. But is there anything else you three could do? Inaya could use some direction and a good head-start on her training. Kailani crosses her arms and thinks. Her eyes trail along the outside foundation of her hut as she considers the question – and, eventually, a light, coy smile starts to spread across her face. "I can think on one thing," she answers. |Inaya really seemed to enjoy spending time with you and Kailani the last time you three went out to train her in how to hunt, and honestly, you think you learned a thing or two yourself. You ask Kailani if there are any other lessons she could teach you both: on top of her being a good teacher, it's a[pc.isDK |n acceptable | wonderful ] bonding experience for you three. "Ah, yes," she answers, nodding her head and smiling so that you can see her pointed teeth. "I am glad you like them too, [pc.name]. And I am glad that you asked!" She tilts her head as she looks at you, her eyes narrowing affectionately. "It is good that you like to learn to hunt, too. It is a good skill to have – and I am glad to teach." ] [rand | Kailani disappears into her hut for just a moment; when she returns, in her hands are half a dozen sticks, each of them carefully whittled of their bark and their surfaces worn smooth. The sticks are worn and weathered, looking as though they've been sitting somewhere in her hut for quite some time; you notice that each of them has one end that's been worn down more than the others, as if something was attached to their flattened ends at one point. They look like they might have been bodies for spears at once point...? None of them are broken, but rather than throw any of her old and used ones out, she kept them stored, maybe for this exact situation. Being on top of a snowy, harsh mountain, good wood that can be fashioned into weapons might be hard to come by. "Come," Kailani says to both you and Inaya, nodding towards the entrance to the village. She has something in mind, but it's not to be inside the village borders, clearly. She leads you a small distance from the village – not so far that Inaya would have difficulty finding her way back, if worse came to worst. It's a widened, flattened area that looks as though it sees a fair amount of traffic on-and-off: the plateau is stamped flat with so many footprints in the snow that it's impossible to discern one from another. On the other side of the plateau is a sheer drop off that goes straight down the mountain, and it's a long way down. On the opposite side, the wall of the mountain reaches higher above you, and the stone wall is dressed with circles of different colors and shapes, drawn crudely directly onto the stone; the chalk is starting to flake and needs reapplying. Near the circles, and especially inside them, the stone of the wall is pockmarked and scratched all over, as if something had been clawing at them over and over. Finally, a pile of flatter stones has been assembled in a neat pile near the stone wall, several paces off in the distance. Kailani gives you two of the sticks, and Inaya the other three, keeping one for herself. "Okay," she says, guiding you to the center of the plateau, with your back to the chasm. Although you're in no danger of falling off the mountain, it still gives you pause, knowing that the drop-off is right there. "[pc.name], this is where vulps... learn to throw the spear." She grips her stick at the halfway point, underhanded; when she lifts it over her shoulder, she spreads her legs and leans back slightly, looking as though she's ready to throw it with all her might. "You must throw the spear and land the point in the marks. You stop when you do not miss." This is how the vulperine hunters get used to the weight of their spears and the strength of their own arms – although these training spears lack sharpened tips, meaning they're unbalanced compared to the spears tipped with metal or obsidian like you've seen Kailani use. Still, the training is good, and once Inaya is older and more confident in her skills, she can graduate to a more appropriate training weapon. You're a quick learner and find that you can be proficient with most weapons given a bit of time, but what Kailani's asking you to do is a little different from what you're used to. Kailani instructs you on how to grip the spear, and how wide your legs ought to be as you ready yourself to throw it. It's a simple posture that you take to naturally, and the motion feels good and your arm feels strong when you throw it, but your aim is constantly off and you have a hard time honing in on how much, or how little, strength you need. Kailani is teaching you a hunting stance, when you're more used to combat stances that emphasize power over accuracy, and on top of that, the wind on top of the mountain alternates between calm and fierce, constantly forcing you to readjust yourself when you think you have it right. Inaya doesn't fare a whole lot better, either: you and her stand the same distance away from the wall, and she needs to put more muscle into throwing the spear than you do, often to worse results. She has a harder time getting back into a proper throwing stance, and when she throws the spear, she either puts too much focus on accuracy and form, or not enough. Still, though, she's having a blast with trying, and you and her make a game out of how many spears you can get into the targets. Green circles are worth one point, while yellow circles, typically higher on the wall, are worth two. She laughs and cheers whenever she gets a point and she gets focused and intense whenever you get one, but really, neither of you are keeping track of how many points you have: what's more important is the time you three are spending together. And even then, the emphasis on scoring points is teaching her body positive habits – the more often she scores, the more often she tries to replicate what worked, and that's going to start working into her muscle memory. She'll be one of the best spear-throwing hunters in the village by the time she's ready. Once Inaya consistently gets into a proper stance on her own, Kailani breaks away from you two. "One more test," she says as she makes her way to the pile of flat rocks stacked neatly on top of each other at the base of the wall. She picks one up, showing you both the flattened side – and scrawled onto its granite is a crude, flaking red circle. "The hunt will not sit still for long. A good vulp ibulim must hit a hunt that runs. Inaya, [pc.name]: try and hit this!" With that, and a flick of her wrist, Kailani tosses the rock lengthwise across the cliff's face, letting it spin through the air with the red circle facing towards you. Neither you nor Inaya were ready for it, and neither of you throw your spear at it. You've already failed: if this were a real hunt, your quarry would have gotten away. There are more rocks in the pile next to Kailani, though, and with another flick, she tosses another flat rock, giving you both a moving target to try and hit. Inaya swings first, and you second, but neither of you land the hit. And to make things harder, Kailani keeps mixing up the angle of her toss, and how quickly they travel: sometimes they go high with a steep arc, and sometimes they're quick and lower to the ground. The constant winds interrupting all three of you don't make things any easier, either. Kailani runs out of rocks to throw before either of you score a hit, but rather than call the practice over, she simply goes to the other side of the plateau, where all the rocks she just threw are, and starts again, tossing them back to the other side. Inaya has three spears while you only have two, giving her an unfair advantage, but it honestly doesn't matter: if she manages to land a strike before you do, it's not because she had one more spear to toss than you did. On one particular toss, [rand |Inaya throws her spear – and the familiar sound of battered, old, flattened wood cracking against stone midair echoes over the plateau, causing the stone disk to wobble and alter its course as it falls to the ground. Inaya had gotten the strike! After a quick celebratory dance, you both agree that that particular hit was worth a million points, and the game is over. |you throw your spear – and the familiar sound of battered, old, flattened wood cracking against stone midair echoes over the plateau, causing the stone disk to wobble and alter its course as it falls to the ground. You managed to get the strike first! But since neither of you agreed on how many points the red circles were worth beforehand, Inaya insists that it's only worth one, meaning that she probably still won the game between you two. ] You help Kailani pick up and stack the rocks one more time for the next group of vulperine hunters that come by. The poor, naked spears will definitely need replacing soon... but in the meantime, that wasn't half-bad practice in teaching Inaya how to hold, aim, and throw a spear. She's one step closer to being a hunter worthy of the name 'ibulim'. | Kailani bids that you follow her. You and Inaya do so as she leads you towards the village's fletcher: a hunter, by the looks of the vulperine at the hut, who's retired and spends their time making hunting weapons and apparel instead. After exchanging a few words (and the retired vulperine gives you a look that you can't immediately discern), the fletcher gives Kailani two bows, as well as some practice arrows: arrow shafts with proper fletchings, but no tips, so that the shafts just end in a dull point. It'd hurt like hell to get shot by them, but it'd be very unlikely to do any permanent damage, even from a trained, practiced archer. The bows themselves look to be proper and well-maintained, although one of them is much too small for you and the string appears stretchier than it ought to be to get any real thrusting power. On the other side of the plateau is a sheer drop off that goes straight down the mountain, and it's a long way down. On the opposite side, the wall of the mountain reaches higher above you, and the stone wall is dressed with circles of different colors and shapes, drawn crudely directly onto the stone; the chalk is starting to flake and needs reapplying. Near the circles, and especially inside them, the stone of the wall is pockmarked and scratched all over, as if something had been clawing at them over and over. Finally, a pile of flatter stones has been assembled in a neat pile near the stone wall, several paces off in the distance. Kailani gives Inaya the smaller bow [var1 |and keeps the larger bow for herself, seeing as you already have one ready. She doles out the practice arrows, giving you and Inaya four each while saving the last two for herself |and gives you the other – it's much larger and better suited to your frame. She doles out the practice arrows, giving you and Inaya five each ]. "Okay," she says, guiding you to the center of the plateau, with your back to the chasm. Although you're in no danger of falling off the mountain, it still gives you pause, knowing that the drop-off is right there. "We learn how to use a bow. [pc.name], you and Inaya must shoot the... the rrumba," she says, rolling the R as she lifts the practice arrow for emphasis, "at the marks. You stop when you do not miss." This is where vulperine hunters go to get used to practice their archery: everything from accuracy to the draw strength in their arms and the strength required to shoot their bows. Although the practice arrows have no tips (and aren't as aerodynamic as a real thing), they're nonetheless a good starting point for a new hunter to get used to how to properly nock an arrow. Once a new recruit gets used to that, they can get started on learning how a proper arrow flies – it'd be dangerous for an archer that didn't know how to prepare an arrow before firing to use real equipment. You're [var1 |already proficient with bows, and you're comfortable enough with your own that firing arrows is like second nature. Most of your shots fire true on the targets – although, you stick with the practice arrows, and there are some growing pains with getting used to how they fly. You can tell from Kailani's own accuracy that she's the exact same way: able to nock and fire them without issue, but her aim is ever-so-slightly off and needs occasional readjustment to hit her targets. |proficient with a variety of weapons, and although you don't typically use a bow, you're a quick learner and take to nocking and firing the arrow expertly after only a few attempts. Your accuracy, however, leaves something else to be desired, particularly since the arrow doesn't quite fly the way you expect it to, given its shape. You can tell that Kailani has some of the same issues: able to prepare and launch the arrow well enough, but her accuracy is ever-so-slightly off with every launch and needs constant fine-tuning. That, and she typically hunts with a spear: her practice with a bow might be a little rusty. ] Inaya, however, struggles quite a bit with her bow. The drawstring requires more strength than she's ready to give it, and she has a hard time nocking the arrow into place: when she gets it upright, it falls out of place, and the few times she does manage to fire it, it flies off in an unpredictable angle, and often sideways (prompting you and Kailani to give her a wider berth than usual). When she manages to pull the drawstring back, her arms shake unsteadily, further throwing off her aim. She holds her breath while taking aim – which is proper form – but she holds it as she's drawing the string, and she holds it for too long, causing her to gasp from exhaustion and release the arrow too soon once more. Kailani is a patient teacher, though. You don't understand most of the words she uses to instruct her daughter, but given her tone, she probably had just as much trouble holding a bow and arrow when she was Inaya's age. Her hands help Inaya set the arrow into place and help her hold the bow up properly; she teaches Inaya that her bow arm needs to be locked straight, and to not bring the fletching of the arrow right up against her eyes. Eventually, after many, many failed starts, Inaya brings the arrow into place; she nocks it properly; she pulls the drawstring back; she closes one eye; she holds her breath as she takes aim; and she lets go. And the arrow flies... mostly straight. It doesn't hit any of the targets, but the bow makes a satisfying 'fwip!' sound as it goes, the bowstring twangs into place, and the arrow, unlike every other arrow Inaya had 'fired' up until this point, hits the rocky surface of the wall with a sturdy, solid impact. "Yay!" Inaya cheers, jumping up and down high enough to bend her knees. She quickly runs over to the arrow she just fired, picking it up and showing it first to Kailani, then to you, in her excitement. The blunted, featureless tip of the shaft is even a bit frayed and splintered from the impact – it was a powerful hit that would have easily pierced the hide of any animal on the mountain, if it was properly tipped. Despite all the practice she's getting, and all the instruction from the best hunter in her village, Inaya's 'successful' shots are few and far between... which makes all the good shots worth celebrating over like she is now. Inaya moves to nock the arrow and try again, but Kailani stops her, putting her hand on the bow's raised edge and lowering it back down. "Wayto ko gillum." She looks to you (and needs to raise her voice a little over the howling winds of the mountain). "We are done for now." Inaya pouts and lowers her bow, holding it lengthwise across her lap – and you can immediately see why Kailani called it off: the fur around the underside of Inaya's left wrist is starting to wear thin. A few more incorrect shots, and the natural bracers of her fur will be torn away, and that'd probably hurt more than the drawstring hitting her wrist by itself. In fact, you're surprised that it isn't bothering Inaya more than she's letting it on. But then again, maybe she's just tough like her mom that way. | "Come," Kailani says to both you and Inaya, nodding towards the entrance to the village. She has something in mind, but it's not to be inside the village borders, clearly. She leads you a fair distance away from the village, well beyond eyesight of its borders, although not off the beaten trail surrounding the mountaintop. The path leading away from the village is twisting and winding, and at times it's thin and precarious, especially with the higher winds – but both Kailani and Inaya walk as though it's not anything difficult or even unusual. Despite their fluffy fur producing so much more drag, they've gotten so used to the conditions in the mountain that even the high winds don't knock them off balance or cause their feet to misstep. You need help walking the path more often than [pc.isDK |a literal child does |either of them do ]. Eventually, Kailani leads you to a large clearing, covered in snow – wait, no, it's not a field: it's a lake. A frozen lake, the ice sturdy enough to support your weight, even fully-geared as you are. Chunks of the lake's icy top has been cut and lifted away, revealing the calm-but-treacherous water underneath. Torn and discarded offal line the banks of the lake, where there's evidence of past temporary shelters having been established. With both of these facts together, you guess that ice fishing is a common method of providing food for the vulperine village. But Kailani doesn't lead you onto the icy surface of the lake (something you breathe a sigh of relief over). Instead, she leads you to one of the lakes several streams feeding into the lake: the water continues to run despite the chill in the air, preventing it from freezing, and the mouths of the streams feeding into the lake go for a small distance before disappearing underneath the icecap. "Fish is an easy hunt," Kailani says – as she steps directly into the running water, barefoot. The thick fur surrounding her feet must give her much, much better insulation than you thought. Or maybe she's just tough as nails. "We can not feed all vulps in the village with just fish. But fish can feed one vulp. It can feed two." She looks to you and smiles, her deep blue eyes vanishing slightly beneath her eyes as her cheeks lift up. "And one mate." Inaya, undaunted and confident, steps into the running stream water with her mother, ready to fish alongside her. [pc.ra vulperine |Despite being vulperine yourself, you're not native to the boreal region and the cold still bites into you; you pass on stepping into frigid water this time. |[pc.hasSkinTags furred |Despite being covered in fur, you |You don't have the advantage of being covered in fur, and you ] aren't native to the frigid, boreal region; you pass on stepping into frigid water and exposing your toes to those kinds of conditions this time. ] You'll just have to watch from the sidelines this time. Swimming through the water and visibly around Kailani's and Inaya's feet are fish: simple, un-exotic trout whose scales gleam underneath the sparkle of the sun reflecting against the water. There's only maybe four of them, and they dart away every time either Kailani or Inaya take a step, but they're quick to reform around their feet, swimming up against the current. "Siln gaus," she whispers to Inaya, patting her on the head gently, as if trying to fine-tune Inaya's stance and position. "Darlum gurd ki fil." Following whatever instruction Kailani gave her, Inaya stays perfectly still in the water: her knees slightly bent with her hands up, palms pointed towards to streaming water. Her tail is up slightly, trying to keep it from falling into the running water, although you can see the strain and effort she's putting in to keep it steady – all of that fur on her tail is awfully heavy. Kailani is just as still and quiet, but she's much more practiced, with her muscles, including her tail, truly kept stock-still as she stands in the water. Both of their stances are wide, with their knees just slightly bent, giving them greater stability against the rushing currents and lowering their bodies just a little bit, bringing them closer to the water. The trout around their ankles start to get complacent, forgetting that two large vulperines had just stepped into their water. Their tail-fins swim and swish through the current, trying to push themselves forward and around their feet – and as soon as one of them gets just a little too close, Kailani whips her hand into the water, her fingers all straightened out so that they slice into the surface rather than batter or slap against it. Just as quickly as it happens, she pulls it out, and in her hand is a wriggling, flopping, slippery fish, desperately trying to break free from her grip and get back into the water she had just yanked it from. The whole action, from start to finish, took maybe as long as it takes for you to blink. "Whoa," Inaya gasps, her eyes going wide at the sight of her mother catching a fish straight out of the stream like that. She lets herself relax enough that her tail dips into the water, causing her to yip and jump in surprise at the sudden chill, something she wasn't prepared for, and that causes all of the fish around her ankles to scatter. Kailani laughs well-meaningly as she gently lowers the panic-stricken fish back into the stream of water, letting it go. It immediately darts back into the lake behind her... although you wouldn't be surprised if it comes right back in a minute. "Like that," she says to Inaya, but her eyes flit up to you to check that you're paying attention. Just in case you ever need to catch a fish straight out of the water with your hands. "Atislin. Aflit. Faelwa yol inglam tag vie." She stands back up and pats Inaya on the head once more. "Try." Inaya's body goes rigid, her tail upright along the stream of the water. She keeps herself as still as can be: everything from not moving a muscle to holding her breath, barely daring to move her eyes along the water's surface to track the fish around her feet. She pauses, trying to get a good bead on one of the trout swimming around her ankles, and she ever-so-slightly starts to lower her body to try and give herself a head-start on catching the fish around herself. That, unfortunately, causes the muscles around her ankles to flex, followed by her calves, and the trout around her legs recognize the minute changes in the water's tension. They don't dart away, but they start to avoid her body, swimming out of reach. If she wanted to catch one, she'd have to extend her arm and lean, which would upset her balance and might even dunk her into the water if she wasn't careful. "Stop," Kailani says sternly, and although Inaya takes her time resetting herself into an upright standing position, she obeys her mother's tone more than her word. "Siln. Gaus." "Gaus ui silntre nah!" Inaya protests in confusion, shrugging her shoulders and waving her hands as if she was trying to barter with Kailani. Whatever it was that Kailani told her to do, it sounded like she thought she was doing it, but is confused on what she's getting wrong. In response, Kailani erupts into a series of sentences, her mouth saying words faster than you can track, with her hands going everywhere from patting the width of her thighs, to the backs of her calves, before swishing her fingers along the surface of the water – and Inaya listens intently to all of it, her brow furrowed in focus as she listens to Kailani's instructions. "Igue," Inaya eventually says once Kailani's done with her teaching, nodding once in resolution before getting back into her wide stance, her knees slightly bent in the water, with her head tilted downwards to watch the trout in the stream. It takes some time before the fish start to gain the confidence to start swimming around Inaya's ankles once more, and once they do, her focus visibly tightens, although she also puts in the conscious effort to keep from moving even the littlest bit, unlike what she had done last time. Before, she bent at the waist to try and give herself a bit of extra leeway; this time, taking whatever Kailani had told her to heart, she stands perfectly, completely still, save for her eyes watching the scales of the trout gleaming underneath the water's surface. She takes a bit more time to ready herself compared to Kailani, but after a few tense moments, Inaya slaps her hand into the water like her mother had, extending her fingers so that they cut into the surface rather than splash into it. Her angle is just a little off, though, and her palm slaps into the water's surface, cutting down on her speed – when she pulls her hand out of the water, she has a fish by the tail, but her grip is weak and the fish thrashes back and forth with just enough intensity that it manages to break free from her grasp. She tries to catch it several times as it falls, but as soon as it hits the water, it's gone. "Laug!" she says in frustration as both of her hands thrust into the water to try and catch the fish, but you and Kailani both know that it's long gone. You're pretty sure Inaya knows it too, but she's trying to put off admitting it. Still, Kailani puts a reassuring hand on Inaya's shoulder, getting her to stop her thrashing in the water for a fish that's not even there anymore. "Good," she says to Inaya. "Next time." As she and Inaya wade out of the water – the droplets in their fur already starting to freeze to icicles as they go, but neither of them showing any discomfort as they walk – you ask Kailani if fish are out-of-season or something. Why did she let her catch go? Was it so there would be more to catch once the seasons change? Kailani laughs, then shakes her head, causing all of the wild hair on her head to sway as she does. "No," she answers honestly. "I just do not like the taste of fish." Oh. That's as good a reason as any. ]"

Soon, ] you're surrounded by other vulperines of the village, many of them bringing instruments of their own: some of them have more drums; some of them have shakers like Inaya; and some of them bring flutes, or simpler instruments like bells. You can tell that none of them have practiced any songs with each other, but music, like dancing, is a language, and one that doesn't need a lot of practice to speak: as long as they all stay on beat, then any kind of noise they make is just music by a different name. If music was a painted picture, then every sound they make is them adding their own brushstroke to the canvas – the end result might be nonsensical and overly busy in some places, but it's nonetheless something everyone made together, as a community. [pc.isDK |And unfortunately for you, you can't really get away with your toe-tapping and your hip-twisting as excuses to dance |And fortunately for you, your inexperience with dancing is just as inconsequential as whether the music was a practiced routine or not ]. Soon, you're pulled away from Inaya to dance with other vulperines, ranging from old to young, with a myriad of different fur colors, and sometimes you're even paired with other [pc.mf | |wo ]men. [pc.isDK |You could follow their lead and try and mimic their actions as they dance, but that feels somehow worse. God, next time, maybe you should keep your damn mouth shut and just tell Kailani that you want to fuck. She's usually pretty willing to fuck when you want to. |Generally, you just try to follow the lead of whoever you're with at the time before they hand you off to someone else, and it's fascinating how many different styles and energies people display as you move with them. It's like you're having whole conversations in the space of a few seconds. ] The trouble with starting a party like this one, though, is that it's hard to know when to stop. The song is improvised, meaning there isn't an 'end' in mind, and you could be trading partners indefinitely the whole time. But the answer is much simpler than that. Throughout it all, Inaya had been shaking her shaker as part of the music. Eventually, she simply stops, and when you look toward her, she's breaking away from the crowd to have a seat. She just got tired of it. And when the song loses one of its instruments, the others quickly follow suit. Kailani and her drum weren't even the last ones still playing by the time everything wrapped up. And just like that, the party is over. You, Kailani, and Inaya had started a whole song and dance party with, near as you could tell, almost everyone in the village, and when one little girl got tired and sat down, it all dispersed. [pc.isDK |And not a moment too soon |That sort of spontaneity is... impressive. You could learn something from being as free-flowing as the vulperine people ]. When it's all said and done, Kailani, with a smile, reaches for you with her hand still grasping the mallet; you put yours in hers, with the stem of the mallet between both of your hands. And Inaya is quick to put her own hand in your other as all three of you head back into the hut[pc.isDK |. At least Kailani's happy. Surely you made some headway with her here. Hopefully it never happens again, though ]. ]
